art37.title: Spain win their second World Cup: La Roja crowned champions after beating Argentina in extra time
art37.lead: Luis de la Fuente's side beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time on Sunday, with a goal from Ferran Torres in the 105th minute, to be crowned champions of the 2026 FIFA World Cup at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. It is La Roja's second world title, sixteen years after South Africa 2010, in a historic final between two Spanish-speaking nations.
body: Match facts

Competition: 2026 FIFA World Cup Final.
Result: Spain 1-0 Argentina (after extra time).
Date: Sunday 19 July 2026.
Stadium: MetLife Stadium (New York New Jersey Stadium during the tournament), East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Attendance: around 80,000, in a venue with capacity for 82,500.
Referee: Slavko Vinčić (Slovenia).
Goal: Ferran Torres, 105' (Spain), assisted by Nico Williams after a cross from Pedro Porro.
Disallowed goals: Nico Williams (97', for a prior foul awarded against Mikel Merino) and Ferran Torres (112', offside).
Yellow cards: Alexis Mac Allister (Argentina, 112').
Red cards: Enzo Fernández (second yellow, 90+3') and Thiago Almada (after the final whistle), both for Argentina.
Line-ups

Spain (Luis de la Fuente): Unai Simón; Pedro Porro, Pau Cubarsí, Aymeric Laporte, Marc Cucurella; Rodri, Fabián Ruiz; Álex Baena, Dani Olmo, Lamine Yamal; Mikel Oyarzabal. Substitutes: Ferran Torres, Nico Williams and Mikel Merino came on in the second half and extra time; Martín Zubimendi replaced Rodri (99') and Eric García came on for Laporte during extra time.

Argentina (Lionel Scaloni): Emiliano 'Dibu' Martínez; Gonzalo Montiel, Cristian Romero, Lisandro Martínez, Nicolás Tagliafico; Rodrigo De Paul, Enzo Fernández, Alexis Mac Allister; Nicolás González, Lionel Messi, Julián Álvarez. Substitutes: Marcos Senesi, Giuliano Simeone and Nicolás Otamendi came on during extra time.
A stalemate settled in extra time

The match, refereed by Slovenian official Slavko Vinčić, reached half-time goalless after a tense first half with few clear chances. In that opening period, Lionel Messi suffered a scare after twisting his right ankle attempting a cross from the byline, though he was able to continue.

The script barely changed in the second half. Spain imposed their possession game and created chances, but ran into a solid Argentine defensive wall and lacked precision in the final pass. The 90 minutes ended goalless and, in stoppage time, Enzo Fernández was sent off, leaving the Albiceleste with ten men for extra time.
Extra time confirmed Spain's total dominance, as they finished the match with 20 shots on target to Argentina's none.
Nico Williams' disallowed goal and the refereeing controversy

The first major controversy of the additional period came in the 97th minute. Nico Williams pounced on a loose ball inside the box and beat Emiliano Martínez, but Vinčić disallowed the goal for a supposed prior foul by Mikel Merino on Otamendi — a stray touch which, according to many analysts, neither prevented the defender from playing the ball nor showed clear intent. VAR did not call the referee to review the incident, which only heightened the outrage on the Spanish bench.

Far from being discouraged, Spain kept pressing and were rewarded soon after: in the 105th minute, Ferran Torres fired home a cross from Pedro Porro in a move started by Nico Williams himself, who made up for his disallowed goal by providing the assist for the strike that won a World Cup. Later, in the second period of extra time, in the 112th minute, Ferran Torres had a second goal ruled out for offside, though the scoreline stayed at 1-0.

In the closing minutes, with Spain holding off Argentina's desperate pushes, Messi himself supplied a ball that Marcos Senesi shot narrowly wide, and Giuliano Simeone spurned a clear chance over the crossbar. When the referee blew the final whistle in the 120+5th minute, Spain were, mathematically, world champions.
A physical battle and a scuffle that overshadowed the celebrations

Beyond the result, the match left behind a residue of tension that Argentina failed to handle well. On the pitch, the Albiceleste racked up fouls and rough challenges for much of the game, with Enzo Fernández picking up a second yellow card in stoppage time and Thiago Almada, who had come on in the second half, involved in several strong tackles.

The most regrettable moment came after the final whistle. In the midst of Spain's outburst of joy, Rodri crossed paths with Nahuel Molina, who made a gesture towards the Manchester City midfielder and sparked a scuffle between players from both teams. Tensions rose further when Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric García by the neck amid the melee, while Gavi, who had come to the defence of his Barcelona teammate, ended up on the ground surrounded by Argentine players. Lionel Scaloni himself had to step in to calm things down, and Thiago Almada was sent off for his part in the brawl.

Argentina's lack of sportsmanship was not confined to the pitch. As Spain began the medal and trophy ceremony, a large part of the Argentine delegation turned their backs on the proceedings and headed to one of the stands to greet their fans, without staying on the pitch to witness the champions' coronation — a gesture that caused considerable controversy in the hours after the final.
Rodri lifts the trophy in New Jersey

Captain Rodri Hernández, named the tournament's best player and awarded the Golden Ball, received the trophy from FIFA president Gianni Infantino and United States president Donald Trump in the ceremony held on the MetLife Stadium pitch. Alongside Rodri, Unai Simón was awarded the Golden Glove as the tournament's best goalkeeper, Pau Cubarsí won the Best Young Player award, and France's Kylian Mbappé took home the Golden Boot as the World Cup's top scorer.
For Argentina, the final marked the end of Lionel Messi's World Cup career with the Albiceleste, a farewell defined by defeat to their eternal continental rivals.
"They are an example for Spain"

A visibly emotional Luis de la Fuente reflected on the title moments after the final whistle: "I feel enormous pride in this generation of players, who have grown with this idea of group, of team, of family. For me it's an absolute honour." With tears in his eyes, the coach from La Rioja added: "They are an example for Spain: together we are stronger."

Goalscorer Ferran Torres did not hide his emotion: "This goal belongs to 47 million people and to the 26 players. It was written in the stars that we'd win away from home, and we wanted them to be proud." The forward, heavily criticised in the months leading up to the tournament, added: "This is a huge release; I've been very criticised, but God always gives me the strength I need."

Back in Spain, the Royal Household congratulated the team in a statement: "World champions! This star is the reward for a journey as long as it was demanding, covered with effort, sacrifice, perseverance and exemplary commitment in every match." The Spanish Olympic Committee also joined the congratulations, noting that Spain "is once again at the top of the world 16 years on."
The party moves to Madrid

The world champions will land in Madrid this Monday from the United States. In the afternoon, the players will visit King Felipe VI and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez before kicking off the traditional victory parade. The route, aboard an open-top bus, will set off at around 20:00 from Moncloa, continue along Calle Princesa and Calle Alberto Aguilera, pass through Plaza de Colón and finish, as tradition dictates, at Plaza de Cibeles, where thousands of fans are already waiting to welcome the new world champions.

art41.title: Xerez, the team that twice held out against LaLiga's Messi
art41.lead: Xerez CD are one of only two teams in LaLiga history to avoid conceding a goal to Lionel Messi, and they did it over two matches, home and away, in the thick of the 2009/10 title race.
body: In a career packed with records, there is one that Lionel Messi never quite completed: scoring against every opponent he faced in the Primera División. Of the more than forty different teams he came up against in LaLiga wearing the Barcelona shirt, very few managed something that neither the best goalkeepers nor the best defences in Europe achieved for almost two decades: keeping a clean sheet against the greatest player in history. Xerez CD are one of those cases, with a detail that makes it even more remarkable: they faced Messi's Barça twice, home and away, in the middle of the title race, and in neither match did the Argentine manage to score against them.
Two matches, a league title at stake

Xerez CD made their Primera División debut in the 2009/10 season, the only one in their history in the top flight, precisely the campaign in which Pep Guardiola's Barcelona and Manuel Pellegrini's Real Madrid fought out one of the tightest league races of the decade, settled practically on the final matchday. In that context of maximum pressure, with every three points weighing heavily in the title fight, the blue-and-whites crossed paths twice with Messi's team.

The first meeting was played on 2 December 2009 at the Estadio Municipal de Chapín, where Barça won 0-2 with goals from Thierry Henry, in the 46th minute, and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, in stoppage time. The return fixture came on 24 April 2010 at the Camp Nou, in the final stretch of the season with the league still undecided, and ended in a 3-1 win for the Catalans: Jeffrén Suárez, Henry and Ibrahimovic scored for the hosts, while Mario Bermejo got the consolation goal for Xerez. In that match, Xerez's Fabián Orellana was also sent off.

In neither of the two games, despite playing the full ninety minutes and despite Barcelona needing to win to stay in the title race, did Messi manage to score against Xerez. No small feat, considering that same season the Argentine would finish as LaLiga's top scorer with 34 goals and Barça would go on to be crowned champions.
The other case: Real Murcia

Only one more case can be added to this statistical rarity in the whole history of LaLiga: that of Real Murcia, who also held out without conceding to Messi, although in very different circumstances from Xerez. The Murcia side only coincided with the Argentine in the Primera División in the 2007/08 season, and in just one match, on the final matchday, played on 17 May 2008 at the Nueva Condomina, where Barça won 3-5 with a Henry hat-trick, but once again without a goal from Messi.

art42.title: Xerez CD hit seven at the Pedro Garrido Trophy in their first pre-season match
art42.lead: Xerez CD thrashed Jerez Industrial 0-7 in the sixth edition of the Pedro Garrido Trophy, the first friendly of the pre-season under Xavi Molist, with goals from Rober Sánchez, Mario Peregrina, Isuskiza, Óscar Lorenzo, Rubén Mesa, Óscar Ganfornina and Isma.
body: The blue-and-whites cruised to victory in the sixth edition of the Pedro Garrido Trophy, a tournament organised by Jerez Industrial, in the pre-season opener for Xavi Molist's side. The coach, with several notable absentees in his squad, shared out the playing time among all his players by fielding two different line-ups and tried out two tactical systems: an attacking 3-5-2 for the first 45 minutes and a more conventional 4-2-3-1 after the break.

To start the match, Molist picked Marcos Alconchel in goal and a back three in the attacking phase made up of Guille Campos, Josete and Manu Rosado, with Jaime Fernández and Chacartegui covering the flanks. Raúl López acted as the team's playmaker, supported by Bittor Isuskiza in the build-up; Zequi and Mario Peregrina operated between the lines, while Rubén Mesa led the attack.
A lightning double in the opening minutes

Barely after kick-off, Xerez went ahead thanks to a goal from academy player Rober Sánchez, who finished unchallenged from a cross from the left by Chacartegui. The second goal came shortly after from Mario Peregrina, who headed in a cross from Rober following a move started by Zequi. The Sanlúcar-born player himself came close to scoring the third with a shot from the edge of the area, but Portela prevented the goal with a great diving save that sent the ball out for a corner.

With Xerez CD in complete control, Molist kept urging his players to move quickly, circulate the ball fast and favour two-touch play against an opponent who were already feeling the strain of their first week of summer training. Portela shone again, this time blocking a point-blank effort from Josete with his face after a corner, in another clear chance to extend the lead on that hot evening of the first of August.

After the drinks break came the third blue-and-white goal, scored by Bittor Isuskiza. Mario Peregrina combined in midfield to break through the opposition lines and laid the ball off to Zequi, who, after flicking the ball over a defender, set it up on a plate for the attacking midfielder to tap into an empty net for 0-3, a goal that drew a big ovation.
A second half with a new-look side

For the second half, Molist made wholesale changes: Fali came into the centre of defence alongside Manu Galán, with David Lachica and Óscar Gallardo on the flanks; Isma and Óscar Ganfornina took charge of midfield; a line of three made up of Zelu, Óscar Lorenzo and Jaime López, with Rubén Mesa as the attacking focal point.

Straight after the restart, Óscar Lorenzo caught the home goalkeeper out with a cross-shot that went into the net. Shortly after, Rubén Mesa pounced on a rebound from the goalkeeper to score the fifth goal of the night. Jaime López wasted the chance to make it six after a great move by Zelu, sending the ball wide.

The sixth goal finally came from academy player Óscar Ganfornina, with a long-range shot that gave the home keeper no chance. David Lachica also had his opportunity after a pass from Zelu, although the Industrial goalkeeper responded with a good save. As the minutes went by the pace of the game dropped considerably, although Xerez rounded off the scoreline with a seventh goal from the penalty spot, converted by Isma, after a foul on Ahmed, a player on trial with the team.
Match facts

Jerez Industrial: Carlos Portela, Manu Jiménez, Daviti, Joselito, Juanjo, Chicho, Manu Rojas, Benítez, Salvi, Mochón and Juanjo Chamorro. Also played: Andrés, Luis, Dani Castro, Pedro, Alberto, Germán, Jorge, Raúl, Javi Romero, Saúl and Beato.

Xerez CD: Marcos Alconchel, Manu Rosado, Guille Campos, Josete, Chacartegui, Raúl López, Isuskiza (Ahmed, 35'), Jaime Fernández, Zequi Díaz, Mario Peregrina and Rober Sánchez. After the restart came on: Carlos Pantoja, Óscar Gallardo, Fali, Manu Galán, David Lachica, Isma, Óscar Ganfornina, Óscar Lorenzo, Zelu, Jaime López and Rubén Mesa.
Goals: 0-1 (1') Rober Sánchez. 0-2 (6') Mario Peregrina. 0-3 (34') Isuskiza. 0-4 (48') Óscar Lorenzo. 0-5 (49') Rubén Mesa. 0-6 (63') Óscar Ganfornina. 0-7 (84') Isma, penalty.
Referee: Patricia Luna Varo.

Notes: Match in the sixth edition of the Pedro Garrido Trophy, held at the stadium of the same name, whose pitch was in poor condition. There was a good turnout in the stands. Before kick-off a minute's silence was held in memory of Borja Ferrer.

art43.title: Xerez CD chain together their second summer win against Ceuta's reserve side
art43.lead: Xavi Molist's side beat Ceuta B 2-0 at La Barca de La Florida and lifted the Andrés Chacón Oñate Trophy, with second-half goals from Jaime López and Mario Peregrina.
body: Second outing, second win. Xerez CD keep building up their pre-season under Xavi Molist and this time lifted the Andrés Chacón Oñate Trophy after beating a stubborn Ceuta B side at La Barca de La Florida. A scrappy match, goalless until well into the second half, which the blue-and-whites settled thanks to a set-piece routine: a corner taken by Zequi that Jaime López headed home to open the scoring.

The Ceuta reserve side, still feeling the physical demands typical of the start of the season, weathered the early storm and grew into the game as the minutes passed, standing up to Molist's men and even getting the better of them in some spells of the second half. However, Jaime López's goal broke the deadlock and settled the result.
First half

To start with, the coach set up a back line with Manu Galán and Josete as centre-backs, flanked by Guille Campos and Chacartegui on the wings. Isma Gutiérrez and Isuskiza shared the holding duties in the double pivot, with Zelu and Óscar Lorenzo out wide, while the attacking pair was made up of academy players Samu Rubiales and Rober Sánchez.

Wearing blue shirts and black socks, Xerez CD went all out from the start, stifling the Ceuta side's build-up play from the first minute. After ten minutes, Nel had to work hard to tip a Guille Campos header round for a corner, and from the resulting set piece Josete went close with another header that flew over. Two warnings that Molist will need to keep polishing, knowing how decisive set pieces are in a division as tight as the Segunda Federación.

Blue-and-white dominance translated into a string of attacks that deserved better luck. Óscar Lorenzo tried his luck with a chip from the edge of the area that hit the crossbar after a slight touch from Nel. Shortly after, it was Zelu who rattled the post with a fierce direct free kick. And before the quarter-hour mark, Chacartegui forced a fine save from the Ceuta keeper with a low, powerful shot.

Ceuta B, for their part, began to venture forward with a few tentative attacks before the drinks break. After the regulation pause, Molist made his first tweak: Manu Rosado came on for Samu Rubiales, which saw Rober Sánchez drop back into the attacking-midfield role and Óscar Lorenzo move up front. Even so, the team lost intensity as the first half went on, having produced their best football in the opening twenty minutes.
Second half

The interval brought a radical change of personnel: Molist made ten substitutions at once, leaving only Guille Campos on the pitch, though moved to centre-back. Opposite them, the Ceuta B side coached by Jerez-born David Álvarez "Polaco" — a team keen to play the ball despite the difficulties of the artificial pitch — used the start of the second half to level things up, a phase in which the blue-and-whites found it very hard to string several passes together and in which the Ceuta reserve side even took control of midfield, an area dominated by Raúl López, Jaime López and Mario Peregrina.

Tempers flared after a challenge by José Miguel on Guille Campos, the prelude to the first goal of the match. Zequi took the free kick and there were protests over an alleged foul on Fali in the area, but play went on and ended in a corner. Once again Zequi delivered the ball into the box and this time Jaime López rose above the defence to power home a header: 1-0.

The referee disallowed a second goal by Mario Peregrina for an earlier offside by Rubén Mesa, a very lively striker throughout his time on the pitch, who forced a turnover that Jaime Fernández almost exploited thanks to his pace, although he could not beat Nel one-on-one. Jaime López himself then had a chance for the second after a pass from Zequi, but his effort went wide. An alert Nel again denied both Zequi and Rubén Mesa in the closing stages. Persistence eventually paid off and Mario Peregrina sealed the final 2-0 close to the end.
Match facts

Xerez CD: Carlos Pantoja, Guille Campos (Salas, 75'), Manu Galán, Josete, Chacartegui, Isma, Isuskiza, Zelu, Óscar Lorenzo, Samu Rubiales (Manu Rosado, 30') and Rober Sánchez. In the second half played: Marcos Alconchel, David Lachica, Fali, Jaime López, Zequi, Mario Peregrina, Rubén Mesa, Raúl López, Jaime Fernández and Ganfornina.

Ceuta B: Nel González, Magno, Naranjo, Juan Esteban, Jon Ander, Goodluck, Abraham Bueno, Antonio David, Owusu, José Miguel and Sergio González. Later came on: Pepe, Suleiman, Adán, Chairi, Miñón, Adrián, Paco Fernández, Pelayo and Pablo Vílchez.
Goals: 1-0 (70') Jaime López. 2-0 (89') Mario Peregrina.
Referee: Antonio Ruiz España, who booked José Miguel and Guille Campos.

Notes: 17th edition of the Andrés Chacón Oñate Trophy, played at the ground of the same name between Xerez CD and Ceuta B, in very high temperatures and with a notable presence of Xerez supporters at the second summer fixture for Xavi Molist's side.

art47.title: Xerez draw with a strong Portuense side
art47.lead: The blue-and-whites post their first goalless draw of the summer, against a side tipped for the Segunda RFEF promotion play-offs.
body: Xerez CD suffered their first setback of the summer last night, though with caveats. At the José del Cuvillo, Xavi Molist's side could not get past a goalless draw against a Racing Club Portuense side that arrives this season as one of the candidates to fight for the Segunda RFEF promotion play-offs on their return to that category. A well-organised, capable rival with good football, who managed to keep a Xerez side still finding its shape in check.

Until now, the blue-and-white pre-season had been nothing but good news. The Xerecistas had won all three of their previous summer fixtures: thrashing Jerez Industrial, a Primera Andaluza side, in the Trofeo Pedro Garrido; beating Ceuta B, of Tercera Federación, comfortably by two goals to nil; and edging past another Group X side, Chiclana, by the minimum. Against the Portuense side in red and white, however, the goal proved elusive for the first time this summer.
A rival that gave no ground

Racing Portuense set out a serious game plan, direct when it needed to be and well organised at the back, and barely conceded a clear chance to a Xerez side that, despite camping in the opposition area for spells of the match, could not find the opening needed to do damage. Neither possession nor the blue-and-white approach play translated into shots of real danger, and the story of the match ended up rewarding the defensive solidity of a side with high ambitions this campaign.

The first half also saw a few rough edges from the home side. As well as being well organised, Portuense were intense in their pressing and made a couple of ill-timed challenges that broke up the rhythm of the game at various points, punished by the referee with two yellow cards, though without unduly affecting the flow of the friendly.

Molist shared out minutes, as has become the norm this pre-season, giving each block 45 minutes as he continues taking notes ahead of the league opener on 6 September. The starting eleven was Pantoja in goal; Guille Campos and Salas at full-back; Moi and Josete at the heart of defence; Raúl López and Isuskiza in a double pivot; Óscar Lorenzo and Zelu out wide; Peregrina as the link man; and Rubén Mesa up front.

After the break, the Catalan coach brought on a block packed with academy players mixed with first-team names: Marcos Alconchel, Gabri, David Lachica, Chacartegui, Manu Galán, Fali, Isma, Zequi, Jaime López, Jaime Fernández, Óscar Ganfornina, Dani Sánchez, Samu Rubiales and Sebas Rubiales all took their turn on the pitch in the second half, without the pattern of the match changing substantially.
A positive takeaway despite the draw

Beyond the result, the reading to take from the match against Racing Portuense is of a Xerez CD still putting the pieces together, with Molist rotating and testing formulas before competition starts to bite for real. This first blank of the pre-season also comes against a rival of real quality, which puts any negative reading of the scoreline into perspective. The blue-and-white side continue their preparations over the coming days, eyes already on the league opener at Estepona on 6 September.

art48.title: Xerez draw against a superior Betis C
art48.lead: The blue-and-whites post their second consecutive draw, this time 1-1 against Real Betis C, in a match that showed the physical toll of two matches in a few days.
body: Xerez CD could not break their run of draws. After Friday's 0-0 against Racing Portuense, Xavi Molist's side shared the spoils yesterday, 1-1, against Real Betis C at the Antonio Gallardo stadium in Arcos, in a match in which the blue-and-whites, with fatigue in their legs from the packed schedule, did not look superior to a lower-category rival that nonetheless plays with real fluency after being crowned División de Honor champions and earning promotion to Tercera RFEF with a squad full of technically gifted players. The Xerez side never quite got going, either in the first half, where Jaime Fernández's forays down the right were the main attacking threat, or in the second, after the usual carousel of substitutions, with Molist still to settle on what looks like his first-choice line-up for the league opener.

The Betis affiliate side, coached by former Xerez man Capi, almost took the lead straight from kick-off. After two minutes, a quick transition caught the Xerez back line out of position and the ball reached Kike, whose shot clipped the post; only a good reaction save from Marcos Alconchel prevented the first goal conceded all pre-season. Xerez responded immediately with a good pass from Jaime López to Jaime Fernández, who raced down the wing and, with space to work with, looked for Rubén Mesa with a cross that fell just short. On eleven minutes the green-and-white affiliate side threatened again: a cross from Zequi to the far post, a knockdown from Chacartegui and an overhead effort from Rubén Mesa that flew over the bar.

Xerez found it harder than expected to build attacks against the intense pressing of a technically excellent Betis C side, who at times forced the Xerecistas to play the ball backwards for long spells of the first half. A foul on Rubén Mesa on the edge of the area led to a shot from Zequi that Víctor turned away with a fine save, a warning sign for the goal that would follow shortly after. Right before the drinks break, in the 26th minute, a bad mistake playing out from the back by the Betis affiliate let Jaime López through one-on-one with the keeper, and he finished coolly into the right-hand corner to make it 1-0.

The blue-and-white joy did not last long. Betis C levelled six minutes later, in the 32nd minute, after winning the ball back in midfield: Casti set up Juan, who finished calmly and gave Marcos Alconchel no chance, scoring the first goal Xerez CD had conceded all pre-season. Molist's side had a chance to restore their lead two minutes after the equaliser, but Zequi's left-footed effort from a great position went wide, and shortly after Jaime López narrowly failed to connect with a header that skimmed the crossbar. Before half-time, Marcos Alconchel again stepped up to deny the 1-2 with a fine save from a shot by Kamará, in another good move from a Betis C side whose sharpest players were Kike, Casti and Juan.
The affiliate side started the second half the better of the two

The Betis affiliate came out of the break much sharper, with Xerez CD sitting back and struggling to play out under green-and-white pressure. Molist, who had already brought on Salas for Chacartegui, soon introduced Guille Campos for academy player Rubiales, deploying him at full-back. In one of Betis's best chances of the spell, Andrew joined the attack and came close to scoring the 1-2, but his effort, taken with an outstretched leg rather than a cleaner header, flew over the bar.

The Xerez coach brought on much of the bench for the final half hour, with chances going begging along the way. Straight after coming on, Samu could have scored after another mistake from the Betis keeper, who gifted the ball to Ganfornina; the academy forward, generously, chose to lay it off to his teammate rather than shoot, and Samu missed a one-on-one that had everything in his favour. A minute later an almost identical move played out, this time with the substitute keeper in goal, and on this occasion it was Ganfornina who went for goal, though his effort was too central. In the closing minutes, Fedir produced a fine save from a good cross by Óscar Lorenzo, one of the last warning signs in a match that gradually lost intensity as it wore on.

The match ended in controversy. In the final play, the referee showed a straight red card to Guille Campos for a foul that was, in fact, in Xerez's favour; to avoid the situation escalating further, the referee opted not to let the free kick be taken and blew the final whistle with the score level.
An imprecise Xerez side with heavy legs

Beyond the result, the match in Arcos left the image of an imprecise Xerez CD, with too many misplaced passes and errors in possession that proved costly against a rival who made the most of them. The physical toll was clear to see: this is now two matches in a row, following Friday's 0-0 against Portuense, in which the blue-and-whites have felt heavy legs in the closing stages of pre-season, a logical wear at this stage of preparation but one that has cost the side freshness and clarity as they continue searching for their best form. Xerecista supporters will hope for an improved showing in the next two friendlies, both at Chapín, before the league opener on 6 September.
Match facts

Xerez CD: Marcos Alconchel, Lachica, Chacartegui, Manu Galán, Fali, Isma, Rubén Mesa, Zequi, Jaime López, Jaime Fernández and Sebas Rubiales. Second-half substitutes: Pantoja, Josete, Salas, Raúl López, Mario Peregrina, Moi, Isuskiza, Guille Campos, Óscar Lorenzo, Gabriel, Ganfornina, Dani and Samu.
Betis C: Víctor, Derek, Kamará, Valero, Andrew, Fran, Nano, Kike, Juan R., Castillo and Casti. Substitutes: Fedir, Gonzalo, Cuevas, Torres, Milko, De Haro, Íker, Juanillo, Everson and Farah.
Goals: 1-0 (26') Jaime López. 1-1 (32') Juan.

Referee: Ignacio de Santisteban Adame, assisted by Raúl Romero and Javi Romero, of the Seville committee. Sent off Guille Campos with a straight red card in the final play. Booked Farah and Ganfornina.
Notes: pre-season friendly played at the Antonio Gallardo stadium in Arcos, with the pitch in perfect condition.

art49.title: The pitch that could break Xerez CD: a ticking time bomb under the squad's feet
art49.lead: The state of the pitch at the Pedro S. Garrido and at Chapín has started to take its toll in the form of injuries and threatens to affect the performance of the city's teams just as the season gets under way.
body: There is a problem in Jerez that has been part of the fans' conversation for far too long and yet seems to find no answer from the institutions: the state of the playing surface, both at the Pedro S. Garrido and at the Estadio Municipal de Chapín itself. It is not a minor issue or simply the complaint of a demanding fan. It is a problem that has already started to take its toll in the form of injuries and which, if not corrected, could end up affecting the sporting performance of the city's teams just as a season full of hope gets under way.

The Pedro Garrido has been dragging along deficiencies in its irrigation system for months, with dry, uneven areas of the pitch that have become a headache for the club in the middle of pre-season. It is no coincidence that, in the height of summer, Xerez CD have had to look into alternatives such as Montecastillo or Costa Ballena to complete part of their training, seeking a more reliable surface to work on. Nor is it a coincidence that Saúl Romero, one of the most exciting signings of the summer, fractured his fifth metatarsal during a routine session on that very pitch. In that particular case the injury may have been caused by a technical movement rather than simply a bump in the turf, but the episode has served to put the spotlight, once again, on facilities that are not providing the reliability a professional club needs.

Moreover, the problem is not limited to the training ground. Chapín faces a reality that few cities in the division have to manage: two teams, each with their own schedules, physical demands and maintenance needs, sharing the same pitch throughout the season. That level of use, often including training sessions, leaves a playing surface that arrives at big matches without the rest or care a competition pitch would need. Any fan who has been in the stands in recent years can recognise the bald patches, bumps and irregularities that appear as the season goes on, especially in the most heavily used areas.

And that is where the part that should truly worry clubs, fans and institutions alike comes in: the health of the players. A pitch in poor condition is not just a question of aesthetics or attractive football. It is a real risk factor. Uneven footing, sharp turns on a surface that does not respond uniformly, areas harder or softer than expected; all of this increases the likelihood of sprains, overloads, stress fractures and muscle injuries that could be avoided with proper maintenance. In divisions where clubs do not always have medical and rehabilitation staff as large as in the Primera or Segunda División, every absence counts double, both in sporting and in financial terms.

Xerez CD have a name and a history that carry weight, a fan base that keeps turning out despite the difficulties and a project that aims to return to the top of Andalusian football. But that effort runs head-on into infrastructure that is not always up to what is demanded of its players every weekend. Investing in pitch maintenance, whether by strengthening the irrigation system at the Pedro Garrido or thoroughly reviewing the state of Chapín, should not be seen as an expense but as a direct investment in the health of Xerez CD's players and, by extension, in the club's sporting performance. The alternative is to keep playing, quite literally, with fire.

The reality, moreover, is that in Chapín's case a simple patch-up will not solve the underlying problem. After years of accumulated wear, what the municipal stadium needs is to have its pitch completely lifted and relaid from scratch, a major project requiring significant financial outlay that, predictably, will not be easy to take on. But Jerez deserves a stadium worthy of its people and its standing, a pitch fit for a city that supports two football projects and, above all, for a Xerez CD whose name and history deserve to play on a surface in proper condition. It is not a whim: it is necessary work that Jerez's institutions should stop putting off.

art50.title: Jaén win the Vendimia and leave Xerez CD with their feet on the ground
art50.lead: Chapín gave its squad a warm ovation before kick-off and turned on it with jeers during the first half, on an afternoon that confirms just how much work Molist still has ahead of him.
body: The party lasted as long as a kick-off. Chapín experienced its most emotional pre-match moment of the summer, with the entire coaching staff and the 26/27 squad paraded out one by one, warm ovations for former Cádiz man Fali and for Saúl Romero, who came out onto the pitch on crutches, still recovering from the fracture suffered days earlier at the Pedro Garrido. But as soon as the ball started rolling, Xerez CD seemed to still be caught up in that sentimental preamble, and a more accomplished Real Jaén side, with the league just around the corner, ran out 0-3 winners in the sixth edition of the Trofeo Feria de la Vendimia.

It was hard to spot a recognisable version of Xavi Molist's side. The scattered approach with which they started the match, perhaps more focused on the pre-match ceremony than on the opponent in front of them, translated into a weak start that the Jaén side knew how to punish without mercy. There were flashes, especially as the minutes wore on, but the unfinished business of a squad still under construction was also on display: a Fali who has yet to convince in central midfield, and a defence that was excessively permissive on the visitors' first two forays into the area.
Two blows and a dressing room going quiet

Jaén did not need to insist to cause damage. On their first attack, a switch of play found Montejano with Salas and Zequi watching the play rather than defending it; the one-two with Mario Martos left the full-back alone inside the area, and his right-footed shot beat Pantoja to make it 0-1. Xerez responded with a run from Salas, sent through by a good pass from Isma, which ran into a Jaén defender, and for several minutes the ball belonged to the blue-and-whites, with the team stringing passes together and looking for space against a well-organised rival.

The calm did not last. A low cross from Busi that nobody managed to cut out ended up at the feet of Peque Polo, who set up Mario Martos to make it 0-2 with a crossed shot. The scorer himself gave another warning soon after with a shot against the post, and the first whistles from a demanding Chapín crowd began to rain down on a nervous side unable to settle on the pitch. Mario Martos, their sharpest player, would end up going off injured before half-time, his right thigh bandaged, making way for Chino.

The other blow of the afternoon came in the form of a physical setback. Isma, up to that point the most composed player in the Xerez midfield, suddenly pulled up with a twinge in his thigh as he started a run backwards, and had to leave the pitch. With that double blow, an adverse scoreline and a costly injury, the sides went in at half-time with a Xerez CD side far from what had been expected.
Xerez find their feet with Isuskiza on the pitch

The change in the script came courtesy of Bittor Isuskiza, who came on for the injured Isma and, with his contribution, began to give the team a degree of order. The transformation was completed at the restart, when Molist reshaped the side with a back three of Guille, Moi and Galán, freed up Salas and Óscar Lorenzo out wide, brought Zequi inside and dropped Peregrina back, leaving Fali and Isuskiza running almost in parallel ahead of the defence. With that new setup, Xerez found their first move of note, with a recovery from Fali, a link-up between Isuskiza and Peregrina and a cross from Guille that Salvi Carrasco claimed without any trouble.

The match then really opened up. A long ball from Manu Galán to Fran Gallego could have cost Xerez a third goal, but Morcillo, clean through on Pantoja, relaxed and let the chance slip. Xerez, buoyed by that let-off, began to find their rhythm: they pushed their lines up, took more risks with the ball and finally offered an image closer to the one Molist has in mind.
The thunderbolt that settled the trophy

The clearest chance for the home side came in the 64th minute, with Zequi carrying the ball and Rubén Mesa waiting alongside him in a two-on-one that came to nothing after an overly long pass. Molist then shook things up with five substitutions at once, bringing on Raúl López, Jaime López, Zelu, Josete and Jaime Fernández, and the fresh legs almost paid off with a free kick from Zelu that Isuskiza headed narrowly wide of the post.

But just as the blue-and-whites were finding their best form, Moha Keita appeared to snuff out any hint of a comeback with a long-range shot that caught Pantoja out: the final 0-3. There was still time for one last Xerez warning, with Jaime Fernández surging past at full speed and striking the post with a shot that had already beaten Salvi. There was nothing more, and the Trofeo Feria de la Vendimia, in its sixth edition, will be heading off to Jaén.

Real Jaén: Salvi Carrasco, Montejano (Pablo, 72'), David Serrano (David Márquez, 72'), José Álvarez (Mauro, 72'), Fran Gallego (Moha Keita, 72'), Adri Paz (Óscar Lozano, 72'), Mario Martos (Chino, 29'), Peque Polo (Morcillo, 46'), Javi Moyano (Mario, 83'), Busi (Caballero, 72') and Álex Pérez (Abel Sánchez, 82').
Goals: 0-1 (4') Montejano. 0-2 (15') Mario Martos. 0-3 (75') Moha Keita.

Notes: sixth edition of the Trofeo Feria de la Vendimia, played at the Estadio Municipal de Chapín. Before kick-off, the coaching staff and squad for the 2026/27 season were presented, and Chapín gave them a big ovation. The mood shifted during parts of the first half, when the stands responded with whistles at the team's poor performance. The pitch was in uneven condition, though somewhat better than in previous matches. A small group of Jaén supporters made the trip to Chapín to support their side.

art51.title: The wrong whistles: pre-season is not the time to demand, it is the time to build
art51.lead: The whistles heard at Chapín during the friendly against Real Jaén reopen a deeper debate: what can be asked of a team that is still very much in the process of being built.
body: Yesterday, in the middle of the Feria de la Vendimia Trophy, Chapín brought out something that has lately become all too common: whistling. It came in the middle of the first half, with the team still taking its first serious steps of pre-season, having been presented to its supporters just minutes earlier amid applause and affection. And there lies the contradiction worth pointing out: the same stands that gave the squad an ovation as they came out onto the pitch greeted them with whistles half an hour later, as if the match were already a play-off final and not a warm-up friendly in which the coach is still trying out pieces, systems and players.

It feels as if we have forgotten what stage of the calendar we are at. We are in August, with the league starting in two and a half weeks, with Molist rotating entire line-ups match after match, with signings who still do not know each other and with a starting eleven that, as of today, is not even the one expected to be first choice. This is precisely the time to make mistakes, to experiment, to concede avoidable goals and for a central midfielder not to quite find his place. That is what pre-season is for. Demanding February's competitive level in August is, quite simply, not understanding the process.

And it is no longer just the result or the performance on the pitch. Now everything is criticised: the shirt, the squad number, the coach's haircut, the order of the presentations. Any detail, however small, becomes ammunition for easy complaint, with hardly any leeway or patience for a project that needs time to settle. It is a phenomenon that is certainly not exclusive to Xerez CD, but in Jerez it hurts especially because of what the club's recent history represents.

Because we should not forget where we have come from. Barely three years ago this crest was stuck in the mud, in the regional leagues, dragging along financial, administrative and structural problems that seriously threatened the club's very survival. Those years taught us the hard way what really matters: that there was a team, that there were fans in the stands and that Xerez CD continued to exist. Everything else, including the logical sporting demands of a division like the Segunda Federación, is a luxury we can afford today thanks to that collective effort to hold on when things were truly ugly.

That does not mean there is no place for criticism, nor that the fans should simply applaud whatever happens on the pitch. Supporters have every right to demand, to analyse and to worry when something is not working. But there are ways and there are moments, and a pre-season friendly, with the squad still under construction, is neither the time nor the place to start whistling. That behaviour does not help the team, does not help the coach and, above all, does not match the road this club has travelled to get back to where it is. It is time to stand by the team, grit our teeth if need be, and save the real demands for when the points truly start to be handed out.

art54.title: Xerez win and impress
art54.lead: Chapín hosts the 11th Rafa Verdú Trophy, with a Zelu goal before half-time deciding a match that was more about the feelings than the result
body: In pre-season the team's progress matters more than the scoreline, and that is the key to reading Xerez CD's win over Juventud Torremolinos, a side from a higher division who start their league campaign next weekend. The 1-0 final score, courtesy of Zelu, confirmed a step forward from the display a few days earlier against Real Jaén, with a particularly inspired Jaime Fernández and with the added bonus of former Xerez player Charaf watching from the stands.
Molist starts to find his team

The blue-and-white coach set the team up from the start with a back three, the big tactical novelty of the afternoon, and also brought back Felipe Chacartegui, now recovered from his muscle problems, on the left flank. The back line was made up of Manu Galán, Josete and Moi, with Jaime Fernández as right wing-back, the position from which he produced one of his best performances of the pre-season. In midfield, the absence of Isma Gutiérrez — who suffered a strain without a tear and is a doubt for the league opener — opened the door for Bittor Isuskiza, who partnered Raúl López; a midfield that worked far better than in previous outings, with far fewer turnovers in the build-up and much cleaner circulation from the back. Jaime López pushed further forward and Zelu appeared more on the left, while up front Rubén Mesa started again, continuing to clock up minutes in the absence of Chuma and Saúl Romero.

Among the crowd at Chapín was former Xerez player Charaf, who closely followed the progress of a team that, with the new back-three set-up, looked considerably more organised and solid than in the previous friendly against Real Jaén.
A heart-stopping start and a Xerez side that grew into the game

The match was not even thirty seconds old when Torremolinos fired a warning after a Xerez turnover: Pau Pérez set up Pinchi on the edge of the area and only a good save from Marcos Alconchel, winning the one-on-one, prevented the first scare.

As the minutes passed, however, the script changed completely. Isuskiza started a press that ended with the ball being won inside the Torremolinos area and a golden chance for Jaime López, who shot with everything in his favour only to be denied by a good response from Javi Cuenca. Shortly after, a well-worked team move between Isuskiza, Rubén Mesa and Jaime López again forced the visiting goalkeeper into action. Jaime López himself, very involved, tried again with a header from a Chacartegui cross and with a long-range shot after again winning the ball off Kaptoum. At the other end, Torremolinos had their best chance when the Cameroonian, a former Betis player, sent wide a ball that had everything in his favour.
Zelu's goal before half-time

Xerez grew in possession, always looking to play out cleanly from the back, with Zelu constantly appearing between the lines while Chacartegui and Jaime Fernández provided width on the flanks. Their persistence was rewarded towards the end of the first half: a long ball from Manu Galán beat the offside trap for Zelu to find himself alone in the area and finish with class, chipping the ball beside Javi Cuenca's right-hand post. A goal that reflected the blue-and-whites' dominance in that spell of the match.
Jaime Fernández, a cut above

If one name stands out from the afternoon at Chapín, it is Jaime Fernández. The blue-and-white wing-back was one of the most decisive players in the match, providing constant width down the right and creating danger every time he took on the Torremolinos defence. His was one of the most eye-catching moves of the first half, when he forced Javi Cuenca into a stretching save after a good combination with Isuskiza and Rubén Mesa, and he also came close to scoring with an effort the Costa del Sol keeper managed to turn away. His dribbling and his runs from deep were one of the main attacking outlets for a Xerez side that, thanks in part to his work, found space in attack more easily.
A dominant second half without further reward

After the break, Xerez stuck to the script. Alconchel was decisive again to keep out a dangerous shot from the edge of the area, and Molist's side had several chances to extend the lead: an effort from Jaime López, who could not control a long pass from Josete, a shot from Javi Mérida that went just past the post at the other end, and further saves from Javi Cuenca to deny Rubén Mesa and Isuskiza, who could not beat the Costa del Sol keeper on the rebound either.

With both teams' substitutes already on the pitch, the match entered an end-to-end final stretch, with Torremolinos looking for an equaliser and Xerez trying to put the game to bed. A late chance for Óscar Lorenzo, which went wide, could have wrapped things up, but the 1-0 held until the end.
Good feelings ahead of the league opener

Beyond the result, Xerez CD leave this trophy having shown a solid image: greater defensive organisation with the back three from the first minute, a much sharper midfield with far fewer turnovers in the build-up thanks to Isuskiza and Raúl López, and a Jaime Fernández who, together with Jaime López and Zelu, emerged as one of the standout and most in-form players ahead of the start of the official competition.
Match facts

Xerez CD: Marcos Alconchel; Manu Galán (Guille Campos, 70'), Moi, Josete; Chacartegui (Salas, 60'), Raúl López (Ganfornina, 80'), Isuskiza (Fali, 70'), Jaime López (Mario Peregrina, 70'); Jaime Fernández (Zequi, 70'), Zelu (Óscar Lorenzo, 70') and Rubén Mesa.

Juventud Torremolinos: Javi Cuenca; Mati, Mérida, Climent; Pau Pérez (Andrés, 72'), Dioni (Buch, 60'), Nico Njalla (Lucas, 60'), Kaptoum (Manu Sánchez, 72'); Pinchi (Iwe, 46'), Petersson (Héctor, 60') and Grozdanic.
Goal: 1-0 (44') Zelu.
Referee: Alberto Sevillano Marín.
Notes: Match in the 11th Rafa Verdú Trophy, played at Chapín on a pitch in poor condition.

art55.title: Xerez rout in Rota, overshadowed by the Salas scare
art55.lead: The blue-and-whites score half a dozen goals at UD Roteña's ground in their penultimate summer run-out, although the day will be remembered for the blow to the head that meant the left-back had to be taken away by ambulance
body: The match left little room for tactical analysis: it was total dominance from start to finish. Xerez CD sealed a comfortable rout at the Manuel Bernal against a UD Roteña side — from the Segunda Andaluza — who also took to the pitch with several players missing due to work commitments. The emphatic 0-6, however, ended up taking a back seat after the scare near the end, when Salas took a blow to the head and had to be treated and taken by ambulance to a medical centre.
Rotation and another attacking display

Molist wanted to spread the minutes, resting Rubén Mesa, who had played the full ninety minutes in the two previous friendlies against Real Jaén and Juventud Torremolinos. In the starting eleven, David Lachica partnered Manu Galán at centre-back, with Chacartegui and Guille Campos on either flank. Fali sat in front of the defence, supported in attack by Mario Peregrina and Ganfornina, with Zelu looking for space centrally and leaving the left flank to Chacartegui. Jaime Fernández stayed out on the right, and up front was Juan Ghia, a player on trial with the blue-and-whites.

Xerez CD's intentions were clear from the first whistle. Barely after kick-off, Juan Ghia had the first clear chance, although the home goalkeeper, Luis, responded well in the one-on-one. The warning became reality very soon after: in the 4th minute, a measured cross from Chacartegui was met by Ghia himself to open the scoring.

With possession entirely theirs and several attacks that did not find the target, Molist's men extended their lead shortly before the half-hour thanks to a spectacular strike from Fali, who placed a direct free kick just under the crossbar, leaving the Rota goalkeeper helpless. The visitors even came close to a third with a Zelu shot that hit the post, but the reward came five minutes before the break: from a corner delivered into the box by Zelu himself, Juan Ghia got the first header and David Lachica tapped in the rebound to make it 0-3, the score at half-time.
Photo: PuroXerecismo
A complete change of team and more goals in the second half

The coach, who had already made a change in goal after 30 minutes — Alconchel for Pantoja — sent out a completely different eleven after the break. The back line was now made up of Moi, Josete, Salas and Sebas; Isuskiza and Raúl López formed the double pivot; Abel and Óscar Lorenzo played on the flanks, and up front were Jaime López and Manu.

This second group of players did not take long to find the net either. Óscar Lorenzo made no mistake from the spot after a foul on Abel inside the area, making it 0-4, and minutes later Jaime López almost extended the lead after a good cross from Salas, although his effort flew over the bar. The match had already lost intensity, practically turned into a training session, when the fifth arrived: a pass from Óscar Lorenzo that Manu converted. The final 0-6 came from Leo well into the second half.
The Salas scare

The good atmosphere of the rout cooled abruptly because of the mishap suffered by Salas, who collided with the opposing goalkeeper shortly after the fifth blue-and-white goal. The player was left hurt after the collision and, a few minutes later, began to feel dizzy, which is why the medical staff decided not to take any risks and called an ambulance to take him to a medical centre. A tense moment that brought the party in Rota to an end.
The anecdote: Fali, besieged by the youngest fans

Amid so many goals, there was also room for the night's heart-warming anecdote. On being substituted, Fali found himself surrounded by a group of children who ran to get a photo or ask for his autograph, causing a small commotion by the touchline that almost prevented him from reaching the tunnel. The midfielder, who had scored one of the goals of the match, stopped to patiently attend to all the youngsters waiting for him.
Photo: PuroXerecismo

Xerez CD: Pantoja (Marcos Alconchel, 30'; Gabi Navarro, 60'); Chacartegui, Manu Galán, Fali, Zelu; Jaime Fernández, Mario Peregrina, Guille Campos, David Lachica, Óscar Ganfornina and Juan Ghia. In the second half came on: Josete, Moi, Raúl López, Isuskiza, Jaime López, Salas, Óscar Lorenzo, Manu, Abel and Sebas. Later, Leo for Salas and Dani for Manu.
Goals: 0-1 (4') Juan Ghia. 0-2 (24') Fali, direct free kick. 0-3 (40') David Lachica. 0-4 (50') Óscar Lorenzo, penalty. 0-5 (60') Manu. 0-6 (75') Leo.
Referee: Saúl González Vargas.
Notes: The match was played at the Manuel Bernal stadium in Rota, on a pitch in excellent condition and with a notable turnout of fans in the stands.

art57.title: Xerez let victory slip in the 92nd minute when they should have wrapped it up earlier
art57.lead: Zelu had put the blue-and-whites ahead before half-time, but a lapse at the back in stoppage time allowed Alfonso to make it 1-1
body: Julio Martínez makes a debut with promising touches, Víctor López gets his first summer minutes and Chuma is still unable to make his debut through injury

Xerez CD missed out on rounding off their pre-season farewell with a win. A goal in the last action of the match ruined a perfect finish for Xavi Molist's side, who had done more than enough to take the win against Atlético Sanluqueño. The blue-and-whites should have settled it in the first half against a powerless opponent, unable to create the slightest danger for much of the match, but the early lead given to them by Zelu vanished in the 92nd minute, when a defensive lapse allowed the hosts to equalise in a game in which the blue-and-whites created chances by the bucketload without managing to put it to bed. It was not a bad performance from the Deportivo, but the lack of finishing up front ended up proving costly, something that from next Saturday, with the league under way, will come at a cost in points.

The fixture also brought two pieces of individual news: Víctor López played his first minutes of the summer, while Chuma is still unable to return from injury. At the other end of the scale, Julio Martínez, the latest blue-and-white signing, made his first appearance and left a very positive impression as soon as he stepped onto the pitch.
A line-up with a league feel

Xavi Molist repeated, give or take a few details, what could be his line-up for the league opener away to Estepona. In fact, this eleven could well be, with some tweaks, the one that starts that official debut. Carlos Pantoja was in goal, while in defence there was a back four with Guille Campos and Chacartegui as full-backs and Manu Galán and Moisés as the centre-back pairing. In midfield, Raúl López and Isuskiza acted as the double pivot, with Mario Peregrina one step further forward. Zequi and Zelu played on the flanks, leaving Rubén Mesa as the focal point up front.

The start was calm, with an early yellow card for Moisés and some flashes from Peregrina, the most active player in that first quarter of an hour. Guille Campos tried to find Zequi with a long ball, but the former Sanluqueño player did not get his body shape right and the home centre-back, sharper in the duel, cleared the danger.
Zelu breaks the deadlock

Possession belonged to the blue-and-whites, although with little penetration and a tempo that suited an opponent — a direct rival this season in Group 4 of the Segunda Federación — who arrived bruised after a heavy home defeat the previous day against Betis Deportivo (0-3). Xerez's main source of joy came down the left flank, more through Chacartegui's runs than Zequi's contribution, although, paradoxically, the first goal stemmed from a Sanluqueño attack that the blue-and-white defence cleared to that same area: the ball fell to Chacartegui again, who put in a cross that Zelu, arriving from the opposite side, turned into the back of the net for 0-1.
Photo: PuroXerecismo

Xerez kept going. Raúl López crashed a volley after a cleared corner just inches wide of the goal defended by Fernando Valencia, and Rubén Mesa forced a good diving save from the home keeper with a long-range shot. The clearest warning of a 0-2 came ten minutes before the break: a diagonal ball from Moisés left Chacartegui completely alone — the most incisive of the blue-and-white attackers in the first half — but he wasted the one-on-one by opting to shoot with his weaker foot, and the effort went wide.

With Xerez still on top, another ball over the top from Raúl López for Zelu caused another scare in the opposition area: the Jerez-born player's cross was looking for Rubén Mesa, but a defender managed to intercept it at the last moment. In first-half stoppage time, it was Guille Campos who fired a warning with a long-range shot that went just past the right-hand post.
More chances after the break, but no reward

Molist changed the line-up at the restart, bringing on Josete, Fali and Marcos Alconchel for Moisés, Isuskiza and Pantoja. The new group came out with energy and within barely a minute had already created two chances: a shot from Zelu, after a lay-off from Rubén Mesa, that was blocked by a defender, and a golden chance for Zequi, who cut inside and sent his left-footed strike just past the post.
Photo: PuroXerecismo

The script stayed much the same: total dominance from Xerez CD, without finding a way to extend the lead. Another surging run from Chacartegui down the left led to a shot from Raúl López from the edge of the area that went just over the bar. Past the hour mark, the match had a tense moment when a clash between the home side's Otero and Xerez's Óscar Lorenzo caused a small scuffle; Ismael, who had leapt up from the bench, ended up being sent off by the referee.

Sanluqueño fired a warning in the closing stages with their first dangerous attack of the match: a good move down the right flank ended with a cross that Otero, completely unmarked, sent over the bar despite having everything in his favour. Shortly before, Julio Martínez had had two perfect chances to open his account for the blue-and-whites, leaving a very positive impression in the minutes he enjoyed on the pitch.
The final blow

The ending came when the result already seemed settled in Xerez CD's favour. Deep into stoppage time, a cross from the right flank was not cleared in the blue-and-white area, and the ball ended up at the feet of Alfonso, who made no mistake to seal the final 1-1. There was no time for anything else.
Photo: PuroXerecismo

Goals: 0-1 (23') Zelu. 1-1 (92') Alfonso.

Referee: Rubén Cartes Burgos, of the Huelva committee. He showed a straight red card to the home side's Ismael (64') and also to the Sanluqueño goalkeeping coach. He booked home players Hugo Moriano and Ismael Salguero, and visiting players Moisés, Óscar Lorenzo, Fali and Víctor López.
Notes: Friendly match played at El Palmar in Sanlúcar, with the pitch in good condition and a notable turnout of Xerez supporters who travelled to the Sanluqueño ground.
Photo: PuroXerecismo

art58.title: A Xerez side that grew into the game drops two points in Estepona
art58.lead: The blue-and-whites hit the crossbar twice, through Moi and Josete, in an intense 0-0 that left a bittersweet feeling in the league opener, made special by the moving saxophone of an Estepona academy player with a Jerez-born father
body: Some draws feel like too little, and the one Xerez CD earned in their league opener at the Muñoz Pérez is one of them. The blue-and-whites hit the crossbar twice and left the Costa del Sol with the feeling that the match had more to offer. A 0-0 that shares the points with Estepona, but leaves in the air that touch of bitterness that only the woodwork produces when it becomes the last barrier before a goal.

Before a ball was kicked, the Muñoz Pérez was filled with emotion. Hugo Castro, an Estepona academy player, took on the responsibility of performing the local anthem on the saxophone, in a scene that gave both sets of fans goosebumps. But the story hid a lovely detail: the young player's father is from Jerez, as Castro himself revealed minutes before kick-off, admitting that his father had "a divided heart today" between his homeland and the colours his son represents. A touch of football's roots before ninety minutes of pure intensity.
Photo: PuroXerecismo
An unrecognisable Xerez at the start

Xavi Molist sprang no surprises and named the expected eleven: Pantoja in goal; Guille Campos, Manu Galán, Moi and Chacartegui in defence; Raúl López, Isuskiza and Jaime López in midfield; and Óscar Lorenzo, Rubén Mesa and Zequi Díaz in attack. Five survivors from last season and five new faces for the official presentation.

The curious part came in the approach. Pre-season had left the image of a team identified with a high press, keen to win the ball high up the pitch and stifle the opponent's build-up, but Xerez came out much more compact than usual, dropping into a mid-block and ceding ground to an Estepona side who were comfortable on the ball in the opening minutes.

The match, with a tense build-up because of the ticketing controversy and the broadcast problems — which left fans unable to follow the game until after the restart — began with two teams of opposing styles. Rubén Mesa fired a warning from the edge of the area (4') and a cross to the far post narrowly eluded Ballarín (7'). Jaime López, one of the standouts of the Xerez summer, got into the area but without luck in his finish (10'), a prelude to Xerez's first clear chance: a ball won by Isuskiza that Óscar Lorenzo turned into a cross which Rubén Mesa could not force over the line (14').

Estepona responded with a header from Ale Contreras that forced Pantoja into action, and the resulting corner again grazed the top corner of the goal. Set pieces, it was already clear, were going to be the main weapon for Manolo Sánchez's side all afternoon.
Photo: PuroXerecismo
A battle with no let-up

The match did not lose an ounce of intensity. A surging run from Rubén Mesa was ruled out for offside (21') while the Deportivo gradually loosened up and gained ground. Moi had to resort to a hard challenge to stop a run into the box, receiving the first yellow card of the match (27'), and the resulting free kick again put Pantoja under pressure. The biggest scare of the first half came in the 34th minute, with a header from Caro after a low cross across the box that had the whole stand holding its breath.

Xerez, however, were not hiding completely: a pass from Jaime López was angled across goal by Óscar Lorenzo and the shot went just past the post (36'), and Guille Campos also fired a warning before the break (45').
Photo: PuroXerecismo
Denied by the crossbar, twice over

After the break, the script barely changed. A foul by Raúl López almost proved costly for Xerez, with a free kick from Ballarín that crashed into the wall (49'). Both benches moved almost in unison: Manolo Sánchez sought fresh legs in attack, while Xavi Molist brought on Julito and Zelu for Jaime López and Óscar Lorenzo.

And it was then that the match turned into a textbook end-to-end affair. In the 65th minute, a great individual run from Zelu down the flank ended in a cross from Rubén Mesa that Zequi missed by centimetres. Two minutes later, Julito hit the post, although the linesman had already raised his flag.

Zelu, who had become the set-piece specialist after coming on, almost caught out Fran Martínez with a good free kick (71'), and barely three minutes later came the first warning from the woodwork: Moi connected with a thunderous strike that crashed against the crossbar from another free kick delivered by Zelu himself, in what looked like the clearest chance of the match.

But Xerez still had one last shot left. In stoppage time, with the match in its dying moments, Josete — who had just come on — repeated the blue-and-white curse and hit the crossbar with another effort, in the play that best summed up the afternoon: a Xerez side that pushed, deserved more and found the woodwork as their only obstacle.
Photo: PuroXerecismo
Penalty appeals at both ends

Estepona, for their part, did not give up either and threatened with three dangerous attacks in the closing stages, as well as appealing for a penalty in the Xerez area (83') that the referee chose not to give. The reply soon came at the other end: the blue-and-whites appealed for one of their own after Julito went down in the opposition area (89'), without the Murcia referee daring to award anything in either case. Two appeals, one at each end, that sum up how tight and contested the match was until the end. Barely three minutes of added time were enough to confirm a draw that feels like too little for a Xerez side that grew into the game and leave Estepona feeling they have dropped two points along the way.
Match facts

CD Estepona: Fran Martínez, Candelas, Heber Pena, Jule Jon, Ariel Herrero (Jorge Álvarez, 56'), Ale Contreras (Samu Expósito, 68'), Ballarín (Nacho Ramón, 56'), Sandji Baradij, Maxi B., Marín and Caro.

Xerez CD: Pantoja, Guille Campos, Manu Galán (Josete, 87'), Moi, Chacartegui, Raúl López, Isuskiza, Jaime López (Julito, 61'), Óscar Lorenzo (Zelu, 61'), Zequi Díaz (Jaime Fernández, 73') and Rubén Mesa (Fali, 73').
Referee: Víctor García Acosta (Murcia committee). He booked Maxi, Ariel Herrero, Caro and Sandji for the home side, and Moi and Raúl López for Xerez.

Notes: First-matchday league fixture in Group 4 of the Segunda RFEF played at the Muñoz Pérez, with more than 200 Xerez supporters travelling to the Costa del Sol. Before kick-off, young Hugo Castro, an Estepona academy player whose father is from Jerez, performed the local anthem on the saxophone in a moving gesture ahead of the match.

art60.title: Xerez CD miss a penalty in the 94th minute and seal their first league defeat against Badajoz
art60.lead: The incidents recorded hours earlier in La Plazuela between fans of both sides clouded a day that had already begun full of emotion with the tribute to Borja Ferrer, the former blue-and-white player who died this summer
body: JEREZ. Football sometimes punishes the small details with real cruelty. And Xerez CD found that out in the worst way possible on a night at Chapín, when Rubén Mesa sent his spot kick straight into Tienza's hands in the 94th minute, burying any chance of rescuing a point that the blue-and-white comeback seemed to have deserved. Xavi Molist's side lost 1-2 to CD Badajoz, the executioner of a league start that has now yielded just one point out of six.
Emotion beforehand and shadows from outside the game

The day began tinged with feeling. Before kick-off, the stadium paid a heartfelt tribute to the much-missed Borja Ferrer, a former player at the club who died during the summer, in a ceremony that moved those present. A minute's silence was also held in memory of all the Xerecista supporters who passed away during the last season, in a build-up full of reflection.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

Not everything off the pitch was good news, however. Hours before the game, it is impossible not to regret the incidents involving supporters of both sides in La Plazuela, an episode that soured the build-up to a regional derby played amid huge expectation, and a reminder that passion, badly channelled, can lead to unwanted events that have nothing to do with sport.
Surprises in the starting eleven

Xavi Molist made unexpected changes to his line-up, bringing Josete into the centre of defence alongside Moi and dropping Manu Galán to the bench after he started the previous week. The midfield was unchanged with Raúl López, Isuskiza and Jaime López, while on the left of the attack the Catalan coach went for Zelu ahead of Zequi. Óscar Lorenzo kept his place on the right and Rubén Mesa continued as the reference point up front.
A script that went wrong early

The hosts hinted at their intentions from the off, first through a Chacartegui cross that ended in a corner as Jaime López was about to shoot, and then with a long-range effort from the same midfielder that went just past the right-hand post of the Badajoz goal.

The game was a tight one, with both blocks well organised and notable difficulty stringing passes together. Molist's players tried to progress with diagonal balls towards Lorenzo and Chacartegui, with Zelu drifting inside, while the Extremadura side built up calmly, although Josete dealt comfortably with Álex Alegría in every individual duel.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Badajoz strike with very little

Jorge Barba warmed up with two long-range attempts —one wide of Pantoja's left-hand post and another with no danger— until at the third he forced the Madrid-born keeper to stretch to the top corner and turn it behind for a corner. From that very corner, Jesús Sánchez arrived unmarked after a poor clearance to connect with an unstoppable header that crept in by the post. A goal that sums up the evening well: the visitors needed very little to strike first.

That blow left the Deportivo reeling, unable to raise their intensity or find answers. The scare could have been worse after a perfectly executed Badajoz counter-attack: Manu Hernández received the ball inside the box, beat Moi with a cut-back and, with the goal already being celebrated, Josete appeared to divert the shot behind for a corner, an intervention that drew the first murmurs of disapproval from the stands.

The hosts' ball circulation became laboured and predictable. Zelu could find no gaps and Óscar Lorenzo frustrated the crowd with his insistence on dribbling rather than crossing into the box. The only attacking option ended up being the ball hung towards Chacartegui, although the opposition defence, well marshalled by Sanlúcar-born Lolo González, neutralised every attempt.
A half-hearted response after the break

Xavi Molist made two changes as soon as the second half began: Zequi replaced Zelu and Jaime Fernández took the place of an unfortunate Óscar Lorenzo. A change of personnel on the flanks, without altering the system.

The Deportivo came out with a different gear and won two corners in barely sixty seconds, cleared by the Extremadura defence amid a tangle of legs. In the 49th minute, referee González Sánchez disallowed an equaliser from Jaime López after a fine move with Zequi, judging that the Sevillian had handled it in the finish.
The second blow, again with astonishing ease

The blue-and-whites were showing a different face, biting into every second ball, enough to reignite the Chapín faithful. Tienza kept out the equaliser with a prodigious save from a low Rubén Mesa shot, during the hosts' best spell. Pushing forward, however, left gaps behind the defence, a motorway for the visitors' transitions.

And that is where the second blow came from. A measured Jorge Barba cross from the right wing found the far post, where Manu Hernández won his position against Guille Campos to beat Pantoja, who got a touch on the ball but could not keep it out. Once again, a goal built with scant resources by the visitors, leaving a deathly silence in the stands, broken only by the chants of the Badajoz supporters.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Despite the setback, Tienza shone again to deny the 1-2 with a feline dive after a Jaime López header, and immediately afterwards held another header from Isuskiza.
The comeback that fell short

Guille Campos went close after a good assist from Zequi, running once more into the wall that Tienza turned out to be, who sent the ball behind for a corner. From that very set piece, Josete and Isuskiza between them finally pierced the visiting goal to cut the deficit.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

Moments later, Zequi had the equaliser on his boot, but his shot went wide of the left-hand post. Xavi Molist used up his options, bringing on Chuma to add another reference point up front and Mario Peregrina to provide control in midfield, withdrawing Raúl López and Jaime López. The Jerez side had another clear chance after Jaime Fernández drove to the byline, although his cut-back was imprecise with Rubén Mesa waiting unmarked to finish. In the closing stages, Chuma received the ball inside the box with Rubén Mesa as the reference point, but his weak shot was repelled by Tienza without too much trouble. Straight afterwards, the Madrid-born goalkeeper and the crossbar combined to prevent the equaliser following a colossal strike from Josete.

The hosts turned into a whirlwind in the closing minutes, with Zequi carrying the attacking load on his shoulders and becoming the most incisive player in the blue-and-white side. Isuskiza tried again without luck, running into Tienza once more. Then came stoppage time, with Jaime Fernández winning a penalty that Rubén Mesa took with a poorly struck effort that the Extremadura keeper saved without great difficulty. There was no time for anything more.
Immediate urgency

Xerez CD drop three points at home, have collected just one of the six on offer and will host Don Benito next Sunday, a side that has won both of its opening two fixtures. The pressure, with the competition barely under way, is already knocking on Chapín's door.
Match details

Xerez CD: Carlos Pantoja, Guille Campos, Moi, Josete (Julito, 90'), Chacartegui, Raúl López (Mario Peregrina, 67'), Isuskiza, Jaime López (Chuma, 67'), Zelu (Zequi, 46'), Óscar Lorenzo (Jaime Fernández, 46') and Rubén Mesa.

CD Badajoz: Sergio Tienza, Edu López, Jesús Ocaña, Lolo González, Mario Gómez, Jesús Sánchez, Álex Alegría (Álex Alegría, 62'), Jorge Barba (Gus, 62'), Guille Perero (Nacho, 69'), Carlos Beitia (Bermúdez, 69') and Manu Hernández (Íker, 84').
Goals: 0-1 (17') Jesús Sánchez. 0-2 (56') Manu Hernández. 1-2 (67') Isuskiza.
Referee: González Sánchez, of the Málaga committee. Booked visiting players Beitia, Jesús Sánchez, Gus and Nacho.

Notes: Second-round fixture in Group 4 of Segunda RFEF played at the Municipal de Chapín, before 8,123 spectators according to the scoreboard. Before the game a tribute was paid to former player Borja Ferrer, who died last summer, and a minute's silence was held in memory of the Xerecista supporters who passed away during the last season. Hours before the match, incidents between supporters of both sides were recorded in La Plazuela, events that it is impossible not to regret.

art64.title: A Xerez side with no ideas and no goals drops points again at Chapín
art64.lead: Xavi Molist's team goes goalless once more against an organised, battling Don Benito, in a match in which the high press worked on in pre-season again proved sterile, with Rubén Mesa disconnected and fresh jeers from the crowd at the final whistle
body: This Xerez CD still cannot find their best version. Nor could they overcome Don Benito, a side who dropped back intelligently and took a point away from Chapín against a blue-and-white team that was blurred, extremely slow, devoid of resources and lacking any finishing. The Jerez side still have not tasted victory after the first three fixtures of the campaign and have barely managed to scrape a single point from their two consecutive outings in front of their own fans. The hosts put in a woeful first half and, although they grew somewhat after the break, above all thanks to the changes introduced from the bench, they fell short. The squad, right now, lacks the necessary confidence and needs to turn around, as soon as possible, a run that not even the most pessimistic supporters had imagined. The next appointment, this coming Sunday, will be at the Nuevo Colombino.
A record unworthy of a contender

Two points out of a possible nine and a single goal scored in three matchdays make up an extremely poor return for a side that aspired to install itself in the upper reaches of the table from the start of the league season. The figures do not lie and starkly reflect the lack of goals and of cutting edge that grips Xavi Molist's team at this start of the season, still a long way from the objectives the club set for this campaign.
A reshuffled line-up

Xavi Molist once again made changes to his starting eleven. Jaime López was left out of the squad due to a knock picked up in Saturday's session; Manu Galán regained his place at the heart of the defence, leaving Josete on the bench, while Zequi was chosen ahead of Zelu. Óscar Lorenzo started again and Mario Peregrina made his first start in the attacking midfield role. The rest of the line-up matched the one that lost to Badajoz: Pantoja between the posts; Guille, Moi and Chacartegui at the back; Raúl López and Isuskiza in midfield; and Rubén Mesa as the sole reference up front.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
High press, no result

The blue-and-whites came out faithful to the script worked on over the summer, replicating the high press that had been the hallmark of pre-season, although once again that approach did not translate into any advantage over their opponents. The match began with Zequi drifting inside to leave the left flank to Chacartegui, thus seeking to exploit his runs. The opening exchanges brought a couple of costly losses of possession from Isuskiza in dangerous areas and a first approach down the right through a cross from Óscar Lorenzo that César Llera cleared without difficulty.
Little football on the pitch

Molist was aiming to recover the version shown in the second half against Badajoz, but intentions are not always fulfilled and the home side put in a very poor first period. Even so, the pattern seemed clear: blue-and-white possession against a Don Benito well set at the back who were looking to strike on the counter. The hosts moved the ball around calmly against opponents who dug in with a back five and four players in front. The first attempt on goal came from Zequi, after a patiently worked move until they found the gap.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

In barely three passes, Don Benito arrived in Carlos Pantoja's area after a rapid transition that Antonio Pavón finished off with a shot that flew just past the right-hand post.
