It was the first warning from the Extremadura side, with much clearer ideas, while the Jerez players found it tremendously hard to trouble the opposition goal, and were also hurried in every action. Zequi tried again with a long-range shot that the visiting defence blocked, sending the ball out for a corner.

The clearest chance to put the hosts ahead came ten minutes before the break: a low cross from Chacartegui that Rubén Mesa failed to reach by a narrow margin. It proved a mirage, however, since the blue-and-white striker remained completely isolated in attack and, despite winning his individual duels against the centre-backs, found himself without support or company. Close to the break, Isuskiza appeared as a saviour to take the ball off Gorka Santamaría when the striker, a former Cádiz player, turned inside the area ready to beat Pantoja. It was the last incident of an awful first half, short on football and without any notable chances of danger.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Pantoja's dive

The Jerez side needed an injection of football and Molist reacted as soon as they returned from the dressing room, bringing on Isma in place of a blurred Isuskiza. It was the second match in a row in which the coach was forced to correct his initial plan at half-time, a clear sign that things were not working. Nothing changed after the restart, and it was Don Benito who came close to opening the scoring, with a left-footed strike from Antonio Pavón that forced Carlos Pantoja to stretch.

The stands were beginning to show impatience with some players, among them Óscar Lorenzo, who was trying without luck. A poor touch that ran away from him out of play exhausted the crowd's patience, and Molist was quick to refresh the attack with Jaime Fernández and Julio Martínez, who replaced Óscar and Mario Peregrina.
A generous Antonio Pavón

The home side improved notably with the substitutions; the ball circulation gained speed with Isma running midfield. Guille Campos tried to catch them out with a shot that Llera saved, and shortly afterwards Rubén Mesa managed to control the ball inside the area, though without any follow-up. Julito also tried his luck with an individual effort, although his shot went straight at the keeper and posed no danger at all. It was Antonio Pavón, however, who spurned 0-1 on a crystal-clear counter-attack after a corner in the hosts' favour: the striker found himself completely alone in front of Carlos Pantoja, who produced a saving hand to repel the visitors' shot. Isma also had another opportunity with an effort from the edge of the box that forced César Llera to turn the ball behind for a corner.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

Molist then brought on Chuma for Moi, switching to a back three, a risky move aimed at chasing the win. Manu Galán, from a considerable distance, hit the crossbar with his shot. The game was entering its decisive phase with everything still to play for, while the Don Benito coach slowed the game down with his substitutions. The hosts poured forward, leaving wide spaces behind them, and the last chance fell to the visitors from a free kick which, fortunately, did not end in a worse outcome for Jerez interests.
Fali, now two matches warming up

Beyond what happened on the pitch, it is a real luxury for Xerez CD to have Fali as an option from the bench, a player who has now spent two consecutive matches warming up throughout the second half without getting any minutes, a sign of the squad depth Molist has at his disposal despite the difficulties with results.
Rubén Mesa, a disconnected striker

Also worrying is the state Rubén Mesa is going through, whose mood appears entirely anxious out on the pitch. The blue-and-white striker, isolated for much of the match and with barely any balls to feed on, reflects in his gestures the lack of confidence gripping a whole side incapable of finding the net in two consecutive home outings.
A curse that keeps repeating

To the misfortune of the scoreline is added a statistic that is starting to feel almost surreal: Xerez CD have now hit the woodwork on five occasions in the first three league matches, a figure that reflects the extent to which fortune is turning its back on the blue-and-whites at decisive moments. The woodwork has become, for now, the particular wall preventing the Jerez side from rediscovering both the goal and victory.
Jeers at the final whistle

The outcome, with two points out of a possible nine at stake, once again provoked the discontent of the Chapín stands, which sent off both the team and coach Xavi Molist with jeers at the end of the ninety minutes, an evident sign of the dismay beginning to settle among the blue-and-white faithful.
Match details

Xerez CD: Carlos Pantoja, Guille Campos, Chacartegui, Moi (Chuma, 76'), Manu Galán, Raúl López, Isuskiza (Isma, 46'), Mario Peregrina (Julio, 56'), Zequi, Óscar Lorenzo (Jaime Fernández, 56') and Rubén Mesa.

Don Benito: César Llera, Raúl Castro, Rubén Sánchez, Keita (Goma, 58'), Carlos López, Antonio Pavón (Mancha, 82'), Copete, Gorka Santamaría (Brian Velázquez, 82'), Philip Osei (Samu Gomis, 85'), Emmanuel and Lolo Pavón.
Goals: None.
Referee: Fernando Moreno Osuna, of the Castilla-La Mancha refereeing committee. Booked Osei.

Notes: Matchday three fixture in Group 4 of Segunda RFEF played at the Municipal de Chapín, with the pitch in irregular condition. Before the match an emotional tribute was paid to former blue-and-white president Joaquín Bilbao. 8,034 spectators.

art70.title: A Xerez side lacking personality brings about Molist's dismissal
art70.lead: An early goal from Ale Marín seals another defeat for the blue-and-whites, the last one the board of directors would tolerate before sacking the Catalan coach just as the fourth league matchday got under way
body: Xerez CD has officially announced the dismissal of Xavi Molist as head coach. The decision comes after the setback suffered at Recreativo de Huelva's ground, a 1-0 defeat that exhausted the patience of the club's leadership and brings the Catalan coach's spell to an end after just four league matchdays.

Molist's departure comes amid considerable institutional unease. His arrival last summer had been presented as a firm commitment to an ambitious project, built around an attacking coach with an attractive style on the ball. However, the numbers recorded during his tenure proved too worrying for the board to keep its patience.
A bitter farewell

Patience has run out. Xavi Molist's cycle at the helm of Xerez CD is over. The Jerez side lost by the narrowest of margins on their trip to the Nuevo Colombino, in a dull game settled by Ale Marín just after kick-off, in the eighth minute. The team is still unable to find its identity, still without a win and still offering no guarantees. The decision, which had been brewing for days within the board of directors, who had already warned the coach during the previous week and put him on the spot, became final as soon as the match ended. Two points out of twelve and a place in the relegation zone sealed his fate.

The blue-and-whites put in a poor showing on the pitch, missing for much of the game despite the changes from the bench, and with very little ability to trouble the opposing goal against a Recreativo side that did not play its best football either, but for whom managing the slender lead was enough. A notable first half and an orderly defensive display in the second were more than enough for the Huelva side.
Three changes to the starting XI, with Fali as holding midfielder

With his future already in doubt, Xavi Molist made three changes from the team that drew goalless with Don Benito last matchday, both in the engine room and up front. The three players with a recent past at the Decano, Manu Galán, Zelu and Rubén Mesa, were all in the starting line-up.

Carlos Pantoja kept his place in goal and the back line was unchanged: Guille Campos and Chacartegui as full-backs, with Manu Galán and Moi in the centre. The big surprise came in midfield, with the inclusion of veteran Fali as defensive midfielder at the expense of the young Raúl López, a regular in the previous league games. Isuskiza continued in midfield, flanked by Zequi and two new faces, Julito and Zelu. Up front, as always, Rubén Mesa led the line.
A difficult start for the Jerez side

With a first-class atmosphere in the Huelva stands, the match began with intensity and mutual respect between both sides. Until the fifth minute the Decano posed no threat, with a move by Paolo that put the ball into the box without Leandro managing a clean finish, in an action that Fali dealt with comfortably.

The home side, however, did not need much more to go ahead. That first warning gave them confidence, and Ale Marín took advantage of a series of lapses in the visiting defence to win the ball and beat Pantoja. It was the eighth minute and things were getting difficult for a Xerez CD side that came into this game with the noose around its neck.

The blue-and-whites were suffering badly and Carlos Pantoja had to work hard to prevent a second in the fourteenth minute, parrying a powerful shot from Ale Marín, the most incisive player on the pitch, after good work from Pol Prats.
A Xerez reaction without reward

The pressure from the Huelva side was suffocating, with a fully committed crowd protesting every action and twice appealing for handball in the opposing box. The Jerez players lacked reaction time in every challenge, although little by little the team settled on the pitch.

Fali became the emotional reference point in midfield, urging his teammates not to lose heart. In the twenty-sixth minute, Zelu won Xerez's first corner, although set pieces would not be the decisive weapon that afternoon in Huelva. Three minutes later, the winger again forced the home defence to concede a corner.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

The Xerez side were gaining ground and, again from set pieces, created chances. A scuffle between Rubén Mesa and Bonaque ended with both being booked and another corner, which Zequi Díaz took without success, although Chacartegui latched onto the rebound with a shot that went just wide of the post.
Another decisive save from Pantoja

The script of the game was partly reversed. Recreativo stopped dominating, but Ale Marín kept appearing out of nowhere, and in the forty-first minute he unleashed a perfect strike from the edge of the area that Pantoja repelled with an outstanding save, preventing a second home goal.

After the scare, Julito tried his luck on his own, coming up against José Carlos. The next corner did sow doubts in the Huelva back line, forcing both the defence and the home goalkeeper to work hard to prevent the equaliser.
A fruitless double change at half-time

Aware that his team needed a spark, Molist left Isuskiza and Rubén Mesa in the dressing room, bringing on Isma in midfield and Chuma up front. The Deportivo gave a warning straight after the restart, with an acrobatic effort from Isma that went just wide of the post, while the visitors appealed unsuccessfully for a possible penalty (46').

Fali prevented the home side's response, clearing for a corner a backheel from Paolo intended for Leandro. In the fifty-fourth minute, Zequi tried his luck with a shot across goal. The Jerez side were gaining ground while Recreativo faded completely, showing clear signs of disconnection.

Xerez CD took control of the game against a subdued opponent, although they found it extremely hard to create clear chances. In the sixty-third minute, Pantoja rescued his side again, this time denying Vela. The home coach, Galván, took that moment to freshen up his team with a double substitution.
Changes without reward

Molist responded to his counterpart's moves with two substitutions of his own, taking off Guille Campos and Zelu to bring on a debutant, Víctor López, and Jaime Fernández. The blue-and-whites, now without Fali on the pitch and with Raúl López as holding midfielder, kept pushing without reward, while the Decano had a chance from a free kick taken by Samu Cortés that Nacho Ruiz headed wide (74').

The home side, despite holding the lead, were far from comfortable, and Galván used up his changes with attacking reinforcements. Xerez CD clung on in the game, and a foul on Jaime Fernández came close to creating danger, although Jero Lario dealt with it with a fine stretching save.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

The clock was running against Jerez's interests and nerves were surfacing on both sides. Recreativo were unable to seal the win, and Xerez CD, despite trying, proved incapable of producing the inspiration needed in the final third, at odds both with goal and with getting the key decisions right. The referee added four minutes of stoppage time, in which the blue-and-whites desperately sought an equaliser that never looked like coming.

The Huelva crowd were calling on the referee to end the match, while Bonaque needlessly complicated matters in an incident that almost sparked tension between both benches. There was no time for more, and Xerez CD did not offer, not even remotely, the reaction that was expected after the run of poor results. The turning point never came, and the consequences were not long in materialising.
Match facts

Recreativo de Huelva: Jero Lario, Néstor Senra, Bonaque, José Carlos, Nacho Ruiz, Alberto Vela (Roan Riera, 84'), Álex Bernal, Pol Prats (Samu Cortés, 64'), Ale Marín (Hugo López, 75'), Paolo (Segura, 76') and Leandro (Agus Alonso, 64').

Xerez CD: Pantoja, Guille Campos (Víctor López, 67'), Moi, Manu Galán, Chacartegui, Fali (Raúl López, 72'), Isuskiza (Isma, 46'), Zelu (Jaime Fernández, 67'), Zequi Díaz, Julito and Rubén Mesa (Chuma, 46').
Referee: Sebastián Roberto Pricopi Gogu (Castilla-La Mancha Committee). Booked Bonaque, Ale Marín, Alberto Vela, Guille Campos, Rubén Mesa and Raúl López.
Goal: 1-0 (8') Ale Marín.
Incidents: Match corresponding to the fourth matchday of Group 4 of Segunda RFEF played at the Nuevo Colombino, with around 700 Xerez supporters travelling to the Huelva stands.

art75.title: Abel Segovia will sign as the new Xerez CD head coach until the end of the season
art75.lead: The coach finally resolves the negotiation process held with the club's board and becomes Xavi Molist's successor
body: Xerez CD will, in the coming hours, bring an end to the uncertainty surrounding its dugout over the past week. Abel Segovia will sign as the new first-team coach until the end of the current season, as has been confirmed, thus closing a negotiation process that had dragged on in recent days. The specific terms of the contract agreed between the two parties are not yet known.
An agreement that finally comes to fruition

The Jerez club and the coach have finally reached an understanding that will allow Segovia to take charge of the Xerez dressing room with the whole of the current season ahead of him, after several days of talks to finalise the terms of his arrival.
Xavi Molist's successor

The new coach thus replaces Xavi Molist, dismissed after the defeat suffered at the ground of Recreativo de Huelva, a result that left the Jerez side with just two points out of a possible twelve and in the relegation places after the first four matchdays of Group 4 of Segunda RFEF.
Imminent debut against Tenerife B

Abel Segovia will have very few days to prepare for his first match in charge of Xerez CD, which will come as soon as next Sunday with the visit of Tenerife B to Chapín. A debut with the added pressure of having to reverse, as soon as possible, a run of results that has set alarm bells ringing among the Xerez fans at the start of the league season.

art76.title: Xerez CD likely to be paired with a Segunda División side, while Recreativo and Lebrijana will face Primera opposition
art76.lead: The criterion of geographical proximity suggests that Recreativo de Huelva and the winner of the tie between UB Lebrijana and CD Ceuta will certainly be drawn against a Primera División side, while the Madrid-based lower-division teams will take the other top-flight representatives, leaving the azulinos without that option
body: The draw for the first round of the Copa del Rey, which will be held next Monday, 5 October, in the Salón Luis Aragonés at the Ciudad del Fútbol, will be governed by the criterion of geographical proximity between the participating clubs, a factor that will decisively shape the pairings in this round.
Recreativo de Huelva and Lebrijana, bound for a Primera opponent

The territorial distribution of the participating teams all but settles that both Recreativo de Huelva and the winner of the preliminary tie between UB Lebrijana and CD Ceuta will certainly face a Primera División representative. As they are the only clubs of standing located in the Andalusian area closest to the big top-flight sides based in the region, the geographical criterion of the draw practically guarantees that top-level tie for both teams.
The Madrid teams, candidates for the other Primera ties

The concentration of clubs based in the Community of Madrid among the lower-division participants suggests, for its part, that the remaining Primera División representatives will be paired with sides such as the winner of the preliminary tie between AD Sporting de Hortaleza and Atlético Unión Güímar, CF Trival Valderas, CDA Navalcarnero or AD Alcorcón, all of them located in the Madrid area.
Xerez CD, with no option of a Primera opponent

This twofold geographical circumstance leaves Xerez CD practically without the option of drawing a top-flight team, as the closest slots are already taken by the Andalusian and Madrid clubs mentioned above. Everything therefore points to the azulinos having to settle for a Segunda División opponent in this first cup round.
Waiting for the final draw

The final composition of the draw groups will in any case continue to depend on the outcome of the preliminary round on 3 and 4 October, so we will have to wait for the coming days to know exactly who Xerez CD will face in its Copa del Rey campaign.

art77.title: A hard-fought comeback: Xerez CD claims its first points of the season against Tenerife B (2-1)
art77.lead: Julito and Chuma overturn Omar Sánchez's opener and give Chapín its first win of the campaign, on an afternoon when the new coach watched the match from the stands
body: CHAPÍN. Jerez was longing for some relief, and Xerez CD gave it to its fans with a win that was hard-fought, worked for and more celebrated than brilliant. The blue-and-whites beat the Tenerife reserve side 2-1 in Abel Segovia's debut, the replacement for the dismissed Xavi Molist, and finally ended their winless run after four matchdays without a victory. Against a young, bold opponent that struck first, the home side's persistence, belief and know-how prevailed.
Segovia begins his tenure from the stands

The first surprise of the morning was not on the pitch, but off it. Segovia, a native of Seville, had to follow the match from the stands: the club has not yet settled the outstanding severance with Molist and, without it, the new coach's registration could not be processed. In his place, Juan Pedro Ramos sat on the bench and led the team.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

Nor was there a revolution in the line-up. Pantoja in goal; Guille Campos, Manu Galán, Moi and Chacartegui in defence; Raúl López joined for the first time this season by Ismael in the holding role; and further forward, Zelu, Julito and Zequi, free to swap positions, with Rubén Mesa up front.
Early momentum, a blow from the reserve side

As almost always happens after a change of coach, the Deportivo came out fired up, pressing high on an opponent that was giving the ball away. Zequi issued a warning from the edge of the box (7') with a shot that went over the crossbar. The Canary Islanders' response came around the quarter-hour mark with a pass from Dylan in behind the defence that Pantoja gathered, and the reserve side gradually shook off the home side's dominance.

The blow came in the 18th minute. After a cross from Sergio Fernández, Óscar Bazaga was through on the goalkeeper and Chacartegui's contact was enough for the referee to point to the spot. Omar Sánchez, the island side's top scorer, sent Pantoja the wrong way with a soft finish to make it 0-1.
A first half in fits and starts

The goal forced the blue-and-whites to regroup, and they did so in fits and starts, without continuity. They pushed with determination, but without finding the final pass or a clean finish. Moi came close to equalising with a header from a Zequi delivery, although the ball went just wide (25').

Meanwhile, the reserve side threatened on the counter. A loss of possession by Raúl López left Bazaga facing Pantoja, who claimed the ball, and the striker did not spot Omar completely unmarked (36'). The first whistles arrived, with Zelu and Zequi switching flanks without finding a way through and an increasingly restless crowd. A fall by Ismael in the box (43') was not deemed a penalty by the referee, and in stoppage time a nearby free kick, won by Galán, was sent over the bar by Chacartegui.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Chuma comes on and the game changes

Segovia, from a distance, needed a change, and Chuma came on for Rubén Mesa, who had been subdued in the first half. Tenerife B, aware of its plan, conceded the ball and territory, leaving the home side without clear routes: neither long balls, nor combination play, nor passes threaded between the lines.

But persistence was rewarded in the 55th minute. Guille Campos cut inside, the goalkeeper parried without holding on and the ball was left loose in a dangerous area. There Julito appeared, alert and well positioned, to tap in the 1-1. The thorniest stretch was over.
Changes, nerves and the decisive blow

Both coaches turned to their benches. Segovia freshened up the attack and midfield, with Peregrina bringing life to the play, and the visiting coach, Mazinho, sought fresh legs for a reserve side that was now less of a threat, although always lurking on the counter-attack.

The reward came from a naive error by the Canary Islanders in midfield. The ball reached Jaime Fernández on the wing, and he put it into the six-yard box, where Chuma, like Julito with the first, made no mistake. 2-1 in the 79th minute. It was the first time this season that Xerez had gone ahead, and the striker, one of the most questioned, lifted a huge weight off his shoulders while Chapín celebrated the joy it had been demanding.

It could have been more: in the 87th minute, Jaime Fernández found himself one-on-one with Gastesi after a great run and angled his shot too wide just as the crowd was already celebrating the third. Zelu also tried, but was exhausted. Five minutes of stoppage time felt eternal, although the three points already had an owner.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Segovia's hand, visible despite the distance

Although he followed the match from the stands, the new coach's style was noticeable in several details of Xerez's play. The most striking was on the flanks. Under Molist, full-backs and wingers positioned themselves very wide, occupying the same lane and reducing space and the ability to unbalance the opponent. Under Segovia, the full-back maintains the width and the wide player moves inside, which created more one-on-one situations and a good number of crosses into the box. One of them ended in Chuma's goal that decided the match.

The work at set pieces was also noteworthy. All the corners were delivered with an inswinging trajectory towards goal, and curiously none targeted the near post, a detail to follow in the coming matchdays.
Final reading

The saying "new coach, guaranteed win" came true. The team needed to win and did so, and that is the main takeaway from the matchday. Segovia still has a lot of work ahead of him, but with a win in the bag and the first touches of change in the play on the flanks, the road begins differently.
Match facts

Xerez CD: Pantoja; Guille Campos (Víctor López, 76'), Moi, Manu Galán, Chacartegui; Raúl López, Ismael (Peregrina, 65'); Zelu, Julito (Isuskiza, 76'), Zequi (Jaime Fernández, 65'); and Rubén Mesa (Chuma, 46').
CD Tenerife B: Gastesi; Joel (Beiza, 84'), Bazaga (Dailos, 66'), Dylan, Ismael, Vila (Amara, 66'), Giovanni, Llorens, Omar Sánchez (Yerovere, 78'), Sergio and Josito (Dani, 78').
Goals: 0-1 (18') Omar Sánchez, penalty. 1-1 (55') Julito. 2-1 (79') Chuma.
Referee: Carlos Agraz Díaz (Extremadura Committee). Booked Chacartegui, Rubén Mesa, Raúl López, Ismael and Julito.
Incidents: Fifth matchday of Group 4 of Segunda RFEF, played at Chapín in front of 7,466 spectators.

art78.title: Xerez CD will face Cádiz CF at Chapín in the first round of the Copa del Rey
art78.lead: The draw held in Las Rozas produced a provincial derby that will, in all likelihood, be played on Wednesday 28 October at the azulino stadium
body: Xerez CD now know their opponent in the first round of the Copa del Rey: it will be Cádiz CF. That was the outcome of the draw held this Monday in Las Rozas from 13:00, in which the azulinos were paired with the yellow side, just as this website anticipated in previous days. The match will be played at Chapín.
A provincial derby in the knockout tournament

The tie pits two of the most representative clubs in the province of Cádiz against each other in a clash with a clear element of rivalry. Xerez, who compete in Segunda RFEF, will have the chance to face a Segunda División side at home, as the criterion of geographical proximity that governs these pairings had already suggested.
Expected date

The match will, in all likelihood, be played on Wednesday 28 October, although the final date and kick-off time have not yet been officially confirmed. We will have to wait for the coming days to know all the details.
A tie with a special flavour

The clash comes at a time when Xerez are looking to recapture good feelings after their first league win against Tenerife B, and it offers the azulino fans the chance to enjoy a fixture of maximum appeal at their stadium, against an opponent of enormous appeal.

art79.title: The last cup meeting between Xerez and Cádiz went the azulinos’ way: a 1985-86 tie settled 4-2 on aggregate
art79.lead: After a one-all draw at the Domecq, Xerez won 1-3 at the Ramón de Carranza, in the last direct Cup tie between the two clubs
body: With the first-round draw of the Copa del Rey now settled and the provincial derby set for Wednesday 28 October at Chapín, Xerez memories travel back to the 1985-86 season, the last time Xerez CD and Cádiz CF faced each other in a direct knockout tie in the competition.
A draw at the Domecq
The first leg was played on 23 October 1985 at the Domecq stadium in Jerez and ended in a one-all draw. The result left the tie open ahead of the clash in Cádiz.
Azulino triumph at the Carranza
The second leg was played on 6 November 1985 at the Ramón de Carranza stadium. Xerez won the derby 1-3 on Cádiz’s ground and sealed their progress with a 4-2 aggregate.
Forty-one years later, a new chapter

More than four decades after that tie, the two sides will meet again in the Cup. This time it will be a single match, with Xerez at home at Chapín. The azulinos, once again cast as the underdog against a higher-division opponent, will try to repeat the feat and feed the hopes of a fanbase that is already dreaming of another derby for the history books.

art80.title: Xerez CD visit Betis Deportivo, a solid leader yet to concede a goal
art80.lead: The azulinos face the verdiblanco reserve side on Saturday at 18:00, a team that has gone five matches without conceding and is the main candidate for direct promotion. A defeat would leave Abel Segovia’s side 11 points behind the leader barely a month into the season
body: Xerez CD face one of the toughest tests on the calendar. On Saturday at 18:00 they will visit Betis Deportivo, leaders of Group 4 of Segunda RFEF, a team that has completed its first five matches without any opponent breaching its goal.
A leader that gives nothing away

The Betis reserve side has built its start on an impenetrable defence. Five matchdays with a clean sheet make the verdiblanco squad a very hard unit to beat and the main contender to achieve direct promotion. Their solidity at the back contrasts with the goal drought the Jerez side endured in the opening matchdays.
A match with a lot at stake

The azulinos arrive at the fixture after opening their win account against Tenerife B (2-1), a result that restored confidence to a dressing room that was going through a delicate moment. With Abel Segovia now in charge of the team, Xerez know the match is worth more than three points. If Betis Deportivo win, the gap to the leader would rise to 11 points when barely a month of competition has passed, a lead that would be very hard to cut. A good result, on the other hand, would keep the azulinos’ hopes alive and confirm that the change on the bench has put the season back on track.
A huge challenge

Beating a team that has not yet conceded a goal is a complicated task. Xerez will need to be clinical in the final third and highly focused at the back. It will be the first big test to measure how far the team has come with its new coach.

art81.title: Jerez City Council urged to finally present Xerez CD with the City Gold Medal, awarded in 2010
art81.lead: Members of the 75th Anniversary Committee denounce, in a letter to the mayor, the "irregular situation" of a full council resolution that remains unfulfilled more than fifteen years later
body: JEREZ. The City Gold Medal that the full municipal council awarded to Xerez CD in 2010 has still not been presented. This is denounced in a letter addressed to the mayor of Jerez, María José García Pelayo, dated August 2026 and signed by Jesús Fernández Aguilar, which calls on the City Council to redress what its authors describe as a "historic injustice".
A request that keeps being turned down

The letter reviews the steps taken so far. In 2023, on behalf of the club’s 75th Anniversary Committee, they held a conversation with the councillor for Sport, who undertook to pass the request on to the relevant bodies. The answer they received was that it was not the right moment.

On 22 July 2024 they submitted a letter through the official channels to formally request that this failure to comply be put right. The mayor then informed the president of Xerez CD of a new negative response, once again based on the situation not being favourable. According to the letter, this increased the weariness and incomprehension of those driving the claim.
"There are no objective circumstances"

Two years later, the signatories maintain that the context has changed. They highlight the current moment of institutional normalisation between the City Council and the city’s clubs, reflected in the agreements recently signed, and state that there are no objective circumstances preventing the club from receiving a recognition granted by the people of Jerez more than fifteen years ago.

They also stress that other relevant people and institutions in the city regularly receive medals, and describe the situation as an "administrative anomaly that is hard to justify" for an institution such as the City Council.
Credit to the current government, but with demands

The letter acknowledges that the current governing team was not responsible for delaying the process, although it considers that the municipal corporation should be the first to ensure that the medal reaches its recipient. It recalls that full council resolutions are binding and leaves open the possibility of taking action if the matter is not resolved, while expressing the wish that this will not be necessary.

"It is my most fervent wish that it will not be necessary for any such action to be set in motion," the text states, trusting that the City Council will show the sensitivity, formality and exemplary conduct befitting an institution that acts on behalf of all the people of Jerez.
Attached documentation
Along with the letter, documentation on the various steps taken and a press dossier have been sent. The signatories are awaiting a response from the City Council.

art82.title: Xerez pay for their physical toll and concede a draw against Betis Deportivo (1-1)
art82.lead: A direct free kick from Chuma made history at the Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol and Rica Funes levelled the scoreline. The referee drove the azulinos to distraction, as they protested two penalties in the verdiblanco box, one on Julito and another on Chuma
body: SEVILLE. Anyone who came to Seville expecting resistance found a Xerez CD full of character. Abel Segovia’s side took away the leader’s clean-sheet record, but accumulated fatigue prevented them from taking all three points. The Jerez side was in control for much of the match, and the Betis reserve team, which had still not conceded a goal, had to wait until the closing stages to secure the draw. The visitors were also left with the impression that the referee had influenced the game: two incidents in the home box, one on Julito and another on Chuma, both claimed as penalties, went unpunished.
Segovia reshapes the attack

The Seville-born coach made changes in the creative zone and up front. An injury ruled out Zequi, whose place was taken by Jaime Fernández, until then an impact substitute and now making his first start. Chuma, scorer of the winning goal against Tenerife B, also started and sent Rubén Mesa to the bench. Julito continued behind the striker, Zelu stayed on the left flank and Raúl López shared the midfield with Mario Peregrina, who was gaining prominence. The back line was unchanged: Guille Campos, Moi, Manu Galán and Chacartegui, with Pantoja in goal once again.

The intention had been announced in the build-up and was carried out from the opening whistle: the azulinos wanted the ball and pressed high to unsettle the build-up play of an opponent, coached by Fragoso, that took more risks than it should have.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Pantoja, the first protagonist

The first scare came from the home side. A cross from Ian ran across the six-yard box without anyone getting a touch until Antonio González, at the far post, struck dangerously. Pantoja, with a prodigious save, prevented the 0-1. Before that, Xerez had already tested the waters with a couple of runs from Jaime Fernández and a cross-shot from Moi following a free kick.
Chuma’s strike

On the right, Jaime Fernández was a nightmare for the verdiblanco defence. On one of his forays, Julito went down inside the box looking for a penalty that González Rodríguez did not award. Shortly afterwards, the same winger won a free kick from Ian Forns on the edge of the area and Chuma, from there, placed a perfect shot that found the net. It was the 24th minute and the first time Betis Deportivo had seen their goal breached in this league.

With the lead, Segovia’s plan kept working: high pressing, ball recoveries and quick transitions. Several times Xerez broke with a numerical advantage, although the final pass was not as precise as the chance required.
The loss of Zelu

Just past the half-hour mark, Zelu put his hand to his left thigh and had to leave the pitch, with Isma Gutiérrez coming on in his place. The setback forced a reshuffle. Betis only responded with a shot from Enzo that went just wide of the post, and Xerez went into the break ahead, with the feeling that they could have had a bigger lead.
A second half of missed chances

Straight after the restart, Peregrina won the ball back, drove forward decisively and played it to Jaime Fernández, who set up Chuma. The latter’s effort went over. A little later, another recovery by Raúl López, one of the best players on the pitch, left Peregrina with an identical opportunity, and the outcome was the same.

Julito could have put the game beyond reach when he was about to go one-on-one with De Pablo, but Rubén de Sá intercepted at the last moment. After that, Curro Macías won the duel against him with an impeccable one-on-one. The reserve side, forced to take risks, left gaps, and the game turned into an exchange of blows.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
The equaliser and the final stretch

With just over twenty minutes left to play, Segovia rested Chuma and Jaime Fernández, both exhausted, and turned to Rubén Mesa and Óscar Lorenzo. Meanwhile, tension was rising on the pitch: the azulino team claimed a second penalty, this time on Chuma, which was not given either, and the atmosphere ended up unsettling Segovia’s men.

In that context, Rica Funes, who had just come on, received the ball on the edge of the area and unleashed a shot that beat Pantoja. Xerez, sitting too deep, gave him space and time. It was 1-1 in the 68th minute.

From then on, the reserve side threw everything forward. Sosu tried a left-footed shot that went wide and Julito, exhausted, missed in a one-on-one. Pantoja shone again with a great dive to stop a powerful shot from Emmanuel, and Manu Galán, on the ground, blocked a venomous effort from Enzo in the last dangerous play. The azulinos held on to the draw, with a very creditable point in the bag before hosting Ciudad de Lucena at Chapín and, after that, Marbella.
Match details

Betis Deportivo: Álvaro de Pablo; Rubén de Sá (Masqué, 85'), Curro Macías, Emmanuel, Ian Forns (De Roa, 85'); Migue Romero, Enzo, Corralejo (Rica, 56'), Antonio González (Rafa Oya, 79'), Borja Alonso (Sosu, 56') and Rodrigo Marina.

Xerez CD: Pantoja; Guille Campos, Moi, Manu Galán, Chacartegui; Raúl López, Mario Peregrina (Jaime López, 79'), Jaime Fernández (Óscar Lorenzo, 63'), Zelu (Isma Gutiérrez, 32'), Julito and Chuma (Rubén Mesa, 63').
Goals: 0-1 (24') Chuma. 1-1 (68') Rica Funes.
Referee: Johan González Rodríguez, from the Tenerife committee. He booked Ian Forns and Rafa Oya for the home side, and Mario Peregrina, Jaime Fernández and Chacartegui for Xerez.
Notes: Matchday six of Group 4 of Segunda RFEF, played at the Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol, with a large presence of azulino fans.

art83.title: Xerez take on a surprising Ciudad de Lucena, who climb to third place
art83.lead: Betis Deportivo, Recreativo, Badajoz, Tenerife B, Don Benito and Estepona have already crossed the Azulinos’ path. On Sunday Ciudad de Lucena, the surprise package of the division after their crazy comeback, come to Chapín
body: JEREZ. Xerez CD remain in the play-out places, but their league position is largely explained by a brutal start to the fixture list. The Azulinos have already faced six sides from the top half, and next Sunday, at Chapín, they will complete the list against Ciudad de Lucena, who have climbed to third place.
A relentless schedule

In just six matchdays, Abel Segovia’s side have faced Betis Deportivo, the unbeaten leaders, Recreativo de Huelva, CD Badajoz, Tenerife B, Don Benito and Estepona. It is a demanding run that has left Xerez with few points but with good feelings in recent weeks, such as the win over Tenerife B or the draw in Seville against the leaders, in which they went ahead through a Chuma goal.
Madness in Lucena
Ciudad de Lucena arrive in Jerez on the best run of their season. The Córdoba side came back from 0-2 down and climbed to third place, a huge surprise that adds to the appeal of the fixture.
A crazy finish in Sanlúcar
The matchday also produced another dramatic ending: Sanluqueño went 3-2 up in the 92nd minute, but their opponents equalised in the 95th to leave the final score at 3-3.
The gaps, still bridgeable

After the matchday, Xerez are 8 points behind the leaders, 7 behind second place and 4 off the play-off places. With Ciudad de Lucena and Marbella back-to-back at Chapín, the Azulinos have the chance to close the gap in front of their own supporters.

art84.title: Segovia’s touch is showing, but Xerez have no margin for error left
art84.lead: Opinion: the team is starting to show a recognisable idea under the new coach, although it needs to build fitness and the league table has stopped forgiving
body: The Xerez CD seen in Seville is no longer the side of the opening matchdays. Under Abel Segovia, the new coach’s touch is starting to show, and so are the shortcomings still weighing on a team under construction.
An idea that is starting to show

The most visible change is on the flanks. The full-backs push wide and provide width, while the wide players drift inside and play between the lines. That formula creates numerical superiority, opens up channels and leads to more one-on-one situations. Against Betis Deportivo, the team started very well, pressing the green-and-whites’ build-up play with intensity and dominating for a good part of the match, up to Chuma’s goal.
A missing level of fitness

But Seville also exposed the problem. The team lasted as long as the fuel lasted. Past the hour mark, fatigue took its toll, the opponents gained ground and Xerez ended up pinned back, holding on. Pressing high demands a level of fitness that the squad does not fully have today, and it is an area where Segovia and his coaching staff have work ahead of them.
Players who are not there yet and others who deserve a chance

The squad is not fully up and running either. There are players who have not yet reached their best level, and others who deserve more opportunities than they are getting. With a new coach and a team in transition, it is time to share out trust with good judgement and reward those who perform.
The margin is narrowing

The biggest problem is not the football, but the fixture list and the points. The poor start to the league has reduced the margin for error. On top of that, Recreativo and Betis Deportivo are not slipping up, which forces Xerez not to drop any more points at Chapín. And also to start picking up points away from home, where they have taken only 2 out of 9, even though in that stretch they have faced three teams expected to be at the top.
Conclusion

There are reasons for optimism in the ideas and the attitude, but the season no longer allows for slip-ups. With two matches in a row at Chapín, Xerez have the chance to turn good feelings into points. From now on, every matchday counts double.

art85.title: Zelu suffers a muscle tear, another significant loss for Xerez CD
art85.lead: The Azulinos’ winger was injured in the 32nd minute of the match against Betis Deportivo and tests have confirmed a muscle tear
body: Xerez CD have a new concern in the treatment room. Zelu has a muscle tear, as confirmed after undergoing medical tests, the injury that forced him off the pitch last Saturday at the Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol.
An injury that was plain to see

The player put his hand to the back of his left thigh and was unable to continue. Abel Segovia had to turn to his bench before the half-hour mark and brought on Isma Gutiérrez. Xerez, who had already gone ahead through Chuma’s free-kick, ended up drawing 1-1 against the leaders.
An important piece in the new Xerez

Zelu had started both matches under Segovia, against Tenerife B and Betis Deportivo, and was shaping up as one of the most prominent players on the left flank of the new team. His absence also comes at a bad time, with two consecutive matches at Chapín against Ciudad de Lucena and Marbella.
Timescales to be determined

For the moment no recovery time has been announced, which will depend on how the injury evolves. We will have to wait for the club’s medical report to find out how many matchdays the winger will miss.

art86.title: Xerez CD to host Marbella on Sunday 25 October at 19:00
art86.lead: The eighth-matchday fixture will be played on Sunday rather than Saturday, as supporters had hoped given the demanding week ahead for the team, with the Copa del Rey derby against Cádiz CF on Wednesday 28th and a trip immediately afterwards.
body: Xerez CD now know the kick-off time of their next league match at Chapín. The blue-and-whites will host Marbella FC on Sunday 25 October at 19:00, on the eighth matchday of Group IV of the Segunda RFEF.
A week without rest

Xerez supporters had expected the match to be played on Saturday, because of the schedule the team faces in the following days. Just three days later, on Wednesday 28 October at 21:00, Xerez CD will host Cádiz CF at Chapín in the first round of the Copa del Rey. After that, they will have to travel to Gran Canaria to face UD Tamaraceite on Sunday 1 November, on the ninth matchday of the league.
Xerez Deportivo FC also at home
That same weekend Xerez Deportivo FC play at home, and that could be the reason why the match against Marbella has not been scheduled for Saturday.
A direct rival in the table

Before that, the blue-and-whites will host Ciudad de Lucena on Sunday 18 October on the seventh matchday. After six matchdays, Xerez CD are 13th with 6 points, one more than Marbella, who are 15th with 5.

art87.title: Four pitches in one week: a challenge for Xerez CD's planning
art87.lead: This week Xerez CD are alternating between the Chapín annex pitch, Chapín, Costa Ballena and San Telmo. Keeping to a routine in a changing environment demands extra effort from the coaching staff and the squad.
body: Training at four different venues in barely seven days is a situation that requires constant adaptation. The Chapín annex pitch, Chapín itself, Costa Ballena and San Telmo make up a map of work that the coaching staff must manage carefully, because each pitch has its own characteristics and can affect the team's preparation. The reason is a lack of availability: the irrigation system at the Pedro Garrido is being repaired, which forces the team to keep changing facilities throughout the week.
Different surfaces, different sensations

Each venue has its own grass, firmness and drainage. Muscles and joints respond differently depending on the surface, so moving from one pitch to another in a few days requires a period of adjustment from the players. Fitness coaches tend to prefer familiar settings in order to adjust training loads more precisely, especially in the most intense sessions.
Planning that adapts on the fly

Physical preparation relies on continuity and progression. When the setting changes, spaces, schedules and exercises have to be readjusted according to what each facility allows. It is a task the coaching staff can handle with experience and flexibility, but it demands more attention and more time spent on organisation.
All of this with an eye on Sunday 18 October, when Xerez CD host Ciudad de Lucena at Chapín at 19:00.

art88.title: One of Xerez CD's bogey teams visits Chapín
art88.lead: Ciudad de Lucena arrive this Sunday (19:00) at a stadium where the sky-blues have left their mark: ten previous meetings, with two Xerez wins, four draws and four Lucena victories
body: One of the most frequent fixtures of the last decade in Andalusian football returns, and for the first time in the Segunda RFEF. Xerez CD will host Ciudad de Lucena this Sunday at 19:00 at Chapín, an opponent they have already faced ten times at home across several divisions and competitions. It is a fixture that has become a regular one, with an intense rivalry, between two teams that have almost always competed for the top places in the table.
Ten meetings at four venues

The meetings between the blue-and-whites and the sky-blues have been spread across the División de Honor, the Tercera RFEF, the RFAF Cup and the promotion play-off to the Segunda RFEF. They have been played at La Granja, the Pedro Garrido, Chapín and the Muñoz Pérez in Estepona.
The record of those ten matches favours the Córdoba side: two Xerez wins, four draws and four Lucena victories.
An opponent that usually leaves Jerez with something

The figures carry an important nuance for Xerez fans. At the various grounds in the city, the matches almost always tipped in Lucena's favour. That is why Lucena are, on their record, one of Xerez's bogey teams in recent years.
Zequi, on the other side in 2022

The reunion also has a curious detail. In 2022, when the two teams met in the promotion play-off to the Segunda RFEF held at the Muñoz Pérez in Estepona, Zequi belonged to Ciudad de Lucena. Today he is a key piece for Xerez CD.
On Sunday, the blue-and-whites have a good opportunity to change that trend, in front of their own fans and with the table getting tighter.

art89.title: Tickets for the Xerez-Cádiz cup tie: 25 to 35 euros and discounts of up to 60 % for members
art89.lead: The club has not provided special or children's tickets for non-members for the provincial derby, so becoming a member is in practice the cheapest way to watch the match at Chapín
body: Xerez CD have announced ticket prices for the Copa del Rey match against Cádiz CF, which will be played at Chapín. A seat in the Tribuna will cost 35 euros, in Preferencia 30 and in the Fondo 25, without discount. Members will pay 20 euros in the Tribuna, 15 in Preferencia and 10 in the Fondo Sur, a discount of 43 %, 50 % and 60 % respectively.
A reduction that changes the sums

The discount represents a notable difference compared with what a non-member supporter will pay. That reduction encourages Jerez supporters who want to attend the derby to become members, the option that works out best for them compared with buying a single ticket. The member price applies until Sunday 25; from Monday 26, all tickets will be sold at the general price.
Cádiz supporters, in the Fondo Norte
Cádiz supporters travelling to Jerez will be placed in the Fondo Norte, and their ticket will cost 25 euros.
No special or children's tickets for non-members

Nor has the club made available special tickets or reduced-price tickets for children who are not members. Members aged up to 14 will pay 12 euros in the Tribuna, 10 in Preferencia and 8 in the Fondo Sur. Families wishing to attend with non-member children will therefore have to pay the general price.
A much-anticipated match

The tie, which pits Xerez against a Segunda División side, is shaping up as one of the most attractive of the season in Jerez. With the match set for Wednesday 28 October at 21:00, the club's challenge now is for the stands to live up to a match of this magnitude.

art90.title: Xerez drew their first meeting with Lucena in front of 400 spectators
art90.lead: On 29 January 2017, on matchday 22 of the División de Honor, the blue-and-whites and the sky-blues met for the first time. It ended 0-0 in front of around 400 spectators at what is now the Pedro Garrido, in a battle at the top of the table that ended with both teams winning promotion to the Tercera.
body: Before the ten meetings in Jerez and the promotion play-off in Estepona, there was a first day. Xerez CD and Ciudad de Lucena faced each other for the first time on 29 January 2017 at the La Juventud stadium, now the Pedro Garrido, on matchday 22 of Group I of the División de Honor. The match ended goalless in front of around 400 spectators.
A battle at the top of the table

Both teams came into the fixture fighting for the top places in the standings. The score did not change throughout the match, which was refereed by Vázquez Hidalgo of the Huelva committee. He booked Guerrero for Xerez, and Troyano, Migue Espinosa and Fede Acuña for Lucena.
Vicente Vargas's eleven

Xerez, coached by Vicente Vargas, lined up with David Zamora; Barragán, Kevin, Álvaro Guerrero, Quirós; Isra, Agus, Juanito Benítez, Alberto; José Vega and Pedro Carrión. In the second half Javi, Abraham, Rubén and, in the 89th minute, Güiza came on.

Ciudad de Lucena lined up with Alberto González; Javi Guerrero, Migue Espinosa, Troyano, Antonio Lucena; Curro Vacas, Sergio Torres, Alfonso Castellano; Erik, Germán del Pozo and Gabri Mayorga. Fede Acuña, Miguel Sanz, Javi Ruiz and Pedro Caballero came on later.
Two promotions and a rivalry

That season ended well for both: Xerez finished third and Lucena fourth, and both were promoted to the Tercera División. It was the start of a fixture that has been repeated many times since. At home, Xerez have ten previous meetings with Lucena, with two wins, four draws and four defeats.
Almost ten years later, the fixture reaches the Segunda RFEF for the first time. On Sunday 18 October, at 19:00, Chapín hosts a new chapter in a story that began with a goalless draw at La Juventud.

art91.title: Xerez sell out Tribuna and Preferencia tickets for the Copa derby against Cádiz
art91.lead: Tickets in the Tribuna and Preferencia for the Copa del Rey first-round match against Cádiz CF, to be played on Wednesday 28 October at 21:00 at Chapín, have sold out eleven days before the match, the club has announced.
body: Xerez CD have sold all Tribuna and Preferencia tickets for the provincial derby against Cádiz CF. Sales opened on Thursday 15 October, with prices of 35 euros in the Tribuna and 30 in Preferencia for the general public, and 20 and 15 euros respectively for members.
Few tickets left in the Fondo Sur
Few seats remain in the Fondo Sur. They cost 25 euros for the general public and 10 for members, a price that applies until Sunday 25; from Monday 26, all tickets will be sold at the general price.
A tie against a Segunda División side

The match pits Xerez, who compete in the Segunda RFEF, against Segunda División side Cádiz CF in the first round of the Copa del Rey. Cádiz supporters have the Fondo Norte reserved for them, with tickets at 25 euros.

art92.title: Lucena leave Chapín as joint leaders against a great Xerez side
art92.lead: A goal from Sergio García a minute from time gave Ciudad de Lucena victory (0-1) in front of 7,832 spectators, in a match Xerez CD dominated from start to finish and in which Abel Segovia's side hit the crossbar twice and saw another effort cleared off the line.
body: Chapín went unrewarded on matchday seven. Xerez carried the weight of the match for ninety minutes, created chances in both halves and conceded almost nothing at the back, but once again ran into their big problem this season: a lack of goals. Ciudad de Lucena, who only troubled Pantoja on a couple of occasions, took advantage of a scramble in the 89th minute to take all three points.
The same eleven, with Zequi for Zelu

Abel Segovia repeated the eleven that earned a point last weekend away to Betis Deportivo, with a single enforced change: Zequi Díaz came in for the injured Zelu. Jaime Fernández, Julito and Chuma formed the attacking line, with Raúl López and Mario Peregrina in midfield.
A dominant first half without reward

Xerez came out with intensity, spreading the pitch wide when building from the back and going for goal as soon as they won the ball in midfield. After five minutes, a run by Guille Campos down the right ended with a Jaime Fernández cross that Zequi sent over. Before the quarter-hour mark, Mario Peregrina played Chacartegui in with a through ball, but Chuma could not get a clean finish on his cross.

The first warning from the visitors came before the half-hour: a cross from Migue on the left took a touch off Isra Cano and almost caught Pantoja out. It was the exception. With Raúl López in control of midfield, Xerez kept attacking down both flanks, although their crosses found no one to finish them. The teams went in goalless at half-time, with the home fans giving their side an ovation.
Crossbar, a goal-line clearance and the crossbar again

The second half began in the same way. In the first minute, Chacartegui pounced on a rebound from a Zequi corner and smashed his shot against the crossbar. In the 53rd minute, a right-footed effort from Zequi beat Hugo, but Rafa Gálvez cleared it off the line. Lucena's only response was a weak shot from Migue from the edge of the area that Pantoja gathered.
Photo: Diario Xerecista

With twenty minutes left, Segovia took a risk: Rubén Mesa and Fali came on for Zequi and Moi, and Chuma and Rubén Mesa played together up front for the first time this season. The change brought Xerez's clearest chance, a lay-off from Chuma for Jaime Fernández, whose angled shot went inches wide of the post. Later, Fali found Chacartegui with a 40-metre pass, without a final finish, and Hugo kept out a shot from Rubén Mesa.
Photo: Diario Xerecista
Five minutes from time, Chuma headed a Raúl López cross against the crossbar, and shortly afterwards Hugo again denied Rubén Mesa, who had turned inside the six-yard box.
The blow in the 89th minute

Just when a draw seemed the likely outcome, a scramble left the ball loose inside the area and Sergio García, who had come on in the 77th minute, scored the 0-1. Stoppage time was not enough. Chapín, who had pushed their side on all match, gave the team a round of applause despite the disappointment.
In their three matches with Abel Segovia on the bench, Xerez have scored three goals and conceded three. After seven matchdays they have 6 points; Ciudad de Lucena move up to 14.
Match facts
Xerez CD: Pantoja; Guille Campos, Moi (Fali, 67'), Manu Galán, Chacartegui; Raúl López, Mario Peregrina (Ismael, 78'); Jaime Fernández (Óscar Lorenzo, 83'), Julito, Zequi (Rubén Mesa, 67') and Chuma.

Ciudad de Lucena: Hugo; Ale Benítez, Rafa Gálvez, Pavón (Porro, 74'), Ortiz, Alberto, Isra Cano (Sergio García, 77'), Manu Molina, Migue (Adrián, 74'), Hugo Fuente (Diego Canty, 62') and Diego Vargas (Joseliyo, 62').
Goal: 0-1 (89') Sergio García.

Referee: Cándido Rodríguez Tavio (Canary Islands committee). He booked Julito (39'), Chuma (51'), Pantoja (79') and Manu Galán (93') for Xerez CD, and Joseliyo (69') and Porro (83') for Ciudad de Lucena.
Notes: seventh-matchday fixture in Group 4 of the Segunda RFEF, played at Chapín in front of 7,832 spectators.

art93.title: What if we asked for help?
art93.lead: Under Abel Segovia, Xerez have gained intensity and judgement, and the squad has the quality for much more. But a team that dominates and does not win is starting to feel the anxiety: perhaps the time has come for the mind to be trained too, and to put every player in his right place.
body: Since Abel Segovia's arrival, Xerez CD have changed their image. The team plays with intensity and judgement, and knows what it has to do on the pitch. They showed it on Sunday against Ciudad de Lucena, in a match they dominated from start to finish and lost in the 89th minute. But the results are not following, with four points out of nine under the new coach, and the feeling is that some players are still not in their right place. One figure sums it up: Xerez have hit the woodwork seven times in seven league matchdays.
Zequi, on his wrong foot

Zequi is a player with real class, but he keeps being played on the left, on his wrong foot. On the right, Guille Campos gives solidity to the full-back position; what is missing afterwards is the cross, that final ball that turns an attack into a chance.
Set pieces, a missed opportunity
There is one resource Xerez are not making the most of: corners and set pieces. Not a single corner is aimed at the near post, a variation that could catch opposing defences by surprise.
Fali, at the heart of the defence

Fali has to play, but at centre-back. On Sunday, in his minutes at the heart of the defence, he showed he has the judgement to bring the ball out from the back. The problem is who to leave out, because all the centre-backs are playing at a tremendous level.
A clever diamond that lacks a spark

In midfield, the team forms a diamond with Raúl López, Mario Peregrina, Zequi and Jaime Fernández. They play with judgement, but perhaps they lack that touch of creativity that Jaime López and Ismael bring. Bittor Isuskiza is a great player, but he is the one you bring on when you want to slow a game down: he brings calm to the midfield.
Up front, between anxiety and effort
In attack, Rubén Mesa is so anxious to score that perhaps that very anxiety is holding him back. And there is nothing to say about Chuma: two league goals, and he gives his all in every match.
The mind plays too

Perhaps it would be a good idea for the team to work with a psychologist, before the players themselves stop believing they can turn the situation around. Because this is a good squad and, little by little, a good team is also being built. There are reasons to trust it. But perhaps the time has come to put every player in his right place.

art94.title: Security operation for Xerez-Cádiz, declared high risk, gets more complicated
art94.lead: The Copa del Rey match between Xerez CD and Cádiz CF, to be played on Wednesday 28 October at Chapín, has been declared high risk by the relevant authorities. In addition, Renfe will not lay on a return train for Cádiz supporters, Cádiz CF has announced on social media, which complicates the security operation and could lead many Cádiz fans to decide against travelling to Jerez.
body: Xerez CD host Cádiz CF on Wednesday 28 October at 21:00 at Chapín, in the first round of the Copa del Rey. The Cádiz club explained in a statement that it tried to negotiate a return train with Renfe for its supporters after the match, but it was not possible. The lack of that train means the security operation planned for a high-risk match has to be rethought.
Fewer away fans
Without a return train, many Cádiz supporters may think twice about travelling to Jerez. The club reserved the Fondo Norte for them, with tickets at 25 euros.
What will Xerez do with the Fondo Norte?

The big question is what Xerez CD will now do with the Fondo Norte seats that may be left empty. One possibility would be to split the stand in two to sell the available tickets on match day. We will have to wait for the club's decision.
Demand for the derby has been high: Tribuna and Preferencia tickets sold out eleven days before the match, and there were few seats left in the Fondo Sur.

art95.title: Jerez City Council to remove the discus throwing structure at Chapín for Xerez-Cádiz
art95.lead: Jerez City Council's head of Health and Sports, Tomás Sampalo, has announced in response to this outlet that the discus throwing structure at the Estadio Municipal de Chapín will be removed for the Copa del Rey match against Cádiz CF, so that there is better visibility.
body: The measure will apply for the Copa del Rey first-round match between Xerez CD and Cádiz CF, to be played on Wednesday 28 October at 21:00 at Chapín. With the structure removed, supporters will have a better view of the pitch.
A match generating great anticipation
The provincial derby has generated great interest: Tribuna and Preferencia tickets sold out eleven days before the match, which has been declared high risk by the relevant authorities.
